feature.bloom.bloom_saturation_tooltip: Controls the color saturation of the enhanced bloom. Lower values make it whiter; higher values preserve or exaggerate its tint.
feature.bloom.bloom_tint_tooltip: Colors the bloom halo without changing the underlying scene lighting.
feature.bloom.compression_ceiling_toolti: The soft limiter's maximum bloom level. Bloom above the compression threshold approaches this value instead of continuing to scale. Set to 0 to remove added bloom.
feature.bloom.compression_threshold_tool: The post-enhancement bloom level where soft compression starts. Bloom below it is unchanged; bloom above it rolls toward Compression Ceiling. Set it equal to Compression Ceiling for a hard cap.
feature.bloom.enhancement_intensity_tool: Multiplies the generated vanilla bloom signal before compression. Raise it to exaggerate weak bloom, such as the sky.
feature.bloom.halo_radius_tooltip: Controls the radius of the enhancement's additional bloom samples. Higher values create wider halos.
feature.bloom.halo_spread_tooltip: Blends between the original bloom and the widened halo samples. Higher values make the halo softer and more spread out.
feature.cloud_relight.cloud_shadows_requ: Cloud self-shadowing requires Cloud Shadows to be installed and enabled.
feature.cloud_relight.description: Relights vanilla cloud textures using the active directional light, cloud self-shadowing, and silver-lining phase lighting.
feature.cloud_relight.key_feature_1: Vanilla cloud color and relit cloud color blending
feature.cloud_relight.key_feature_3: Directional cloud self-shadowing from the active sun or moon
feature.cloud_relight.name: Cloud Relight
feature.cloud_relight.relight_mix_toolti: Multiplier on the directional light contribution added to clouds.
feature.cloud_relight.silver_lining_acce: Strength of the broad glow and sharp silver lining added to the cloud body. Does not reduce body lighting.
feature.cloud_relight.silver_lining_spre:
Positive: silver lining spreads into thicker cloud areas.
Negative: silver lining is confined to thinner cloud edges.
feature.cloud_relight.vanilla_mix_toolti: Multiplier on the original vanilla cloud color before relighting is applied.

feature.cloud_shadows.key_feature_1: Dynamic cloud shadow projection on terrain and objects
feature.cloud_shadows.key_feature_2: Configurable shadow opacity for artistic control
feature.cloud_shadows.key_feature_3: Real-time shadow movement synchronized with cloud motion
feature.cloud_shadows.key_feature_4: Cubemap-based shadow calculation for accurate projection

Uses ambient lighting, including IBL when enabled, plus shadowed directional light for the color and brightness of effect meshes and sky statics. Separate brightness controls still apply.
feature.cs_utility.description: Core utility controls for shared renderer tuning.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_blur_multipl: Scales Near Blur and Far Blur. This matches Skyrim's Settings > Display > Depth of Field slider and fDynamicDOFBlurMultiplier.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_far_blur_too: Far-side blur amount before the game slider multiplier is applied.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_far_distance: Offset before pixels farther than the sampled focus depth begin to blur.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_far_range_to: Fade width for far-side blur. Higher values make the transition into blur more gradual.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_focus_settin: Auto Focus uses Skyrim's cached dynamic DOF values. The vanilla Display Depth of Field slider maps to Game Slider / Multiplier.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_focus_toolti: Uses Skyrim's dynamic DOF path, which shifts focus from the sampled scene depth. bDoDepthOfField can still disable the effect, and fDDOFFocusCenterweightExt changes sample weighting.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_near_blur_to: Near-side blur amount before the game slider multiplier is applied.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_near_distanc: Offset before pixels nearer than the sampled focus depth begin to blur.
feature.cs_utility.dof_auto_near_range_t: Fade width for near-side blur. Higher values make the transition into blur more gradual.
feature.cs_utility.dof_distance_tooltip: Static focus distance. Mode decides whether blur applies in front of it, behind it, both, or neither.
feature.cs_utility.dof_exclude_sky_toolt: Sets the No Sky flag so the sky is excluded from the DOF blur pass.
feature.cs_utility.dof_lock_popup_messag: Discard the manual depth of field values and lock controls to live image space values?
feature.cs_utility.dof_lock_tooltip: Lock depth of field controls to live image space values.
feature.cs_utility.dof_range_tooltip: Static transition width around Distance. Higher values make blur fade in more gradually.
feature.cs_utility.dof_reset_tooltip: Reset to current live image space values without changing the lock state.
feature.cs_utility.dof_scene_no_data: No live scene image space data is available.
feature.cs_utility.dof_underwater_no_dat: No underwater image space record is currently applied.
feature.cs_utility.dof_unlock_tooltip: Unlock depth of field for manual editing.
feature.cs_utility.dof_unlock_unavailabl: No live image space values are available.
feature.cs_utility.effect_brightness_too: Scales effect lighting from the weather or ambient lighting. One preserves its brightness; lower values darken it and higher values brighten it.
feature.cs_utility.effect_lighting_multi: Adjusts lighting on effect meshes according to their lighting influence.
feature.cs_utility.fog_intensity_tooltip: Scales vanilla distance fog opacity. Zero removes it; one preserves its current strength. Has no effect when Exponential Height Fog disables vanilla fog.
feature.cs_utility.fog_transparency_gamm: Adjusts vanilla distance fog opacity. Negative values make fog denser; positive values make it more transparent.
feature.cs_utility.gamma_offset_tooltip: Adjusts the brightness curve. Negative values lift midtones; positive values lower them. Zero preserves the current curve.
feature.cs_utility.key_feature_3: Separate controls for linear point lights
feature.cs_utility.linear_slider_disable: Enable Linear Lighting to use these controls.
feature.cs_utility.name: BF Utility
feature.cs_utility.scene_brightness_tool: Adjusts lighting and atmosphere together. One preserves the individual controls; lower values darken the scene and higher values brighten it.
feature.cs_utility.sky_saturation_toolti: Zero makes the sky grayscale. One preserves the current colors; higher values increase saturation.
feature.cs_utility.sky_static_brightness: Scales sky static lighting from the weather or ambient lighting. One preserves its brightness; lower values darken it and higher values brighten it.
feature.cs_utility.sky_static_transparen: Fades sky static meshes. Zero preserves their current visibility; one makes them fully transparent.
feature.cs_utility.water_brightness_tool: Scales the final water surface brightness.
feature.cs_utility.water_caustics_disper: Scales the separation of colors in caustics. Zero removes color separation.
feature.cs_utility.water_caustics_speed_: Scales caustics animation speed. Zero freezes the pattern.
feature.cs_utility.water_caustics_streng: Scales the underwater light pattern contrast. One preserves the current appearance; zero disables caustics.
feature.cs_utility.water_caustics_tiling: Scales how often the caustics pattern repeats. Higher values create smaller patterns.
feature.cs_utility.water_fresnel_max_too: Maximum reflection response at grazing view angles.
feature.cs_utility.water_fresnel_min_too: Minimum reflection response when viewing the water surface head-on.
feature.cs_utility.water_muddiness_toolt: Scales the water tint mixed over the refracted scene. Lower values make water clearer.
feature.cs_utility.water_parallax_qualit: Sets water parallax sampling quality, including flowmaps. 16 matches current quality. Higher values reduce stepping and increase GPU cost.
feature.cs_utility.water_parallax_streng: Scales the apparent depth of water waves, including flowmaps. One preserves the current appearance; zero disables water parallax.
feature.cs_utility.water_reflection_amou: Scales environment, cubemap, and screen-space reflections on water.
feature.cs_utility.water_refraction_amou: Scales the distortion applied to the scene viewed through water.
feature.cs_utility.water_sun_specular_mu: Scales the direct sun highlight reflected by the water surface.
feature.cs_utility.water_wave_amplitude_: Scales water surface normals, including flowmap and rain ripple detail.

feature.dynamic_cubemaps.key_feature_1: Real-time environment capture for realistic reflections
feature.dynamic_cubemaps.key_feature_2: Dynamic cube map generation based on camera position
feature.dynamic_cubemaps.key_feature_3: Enhanced water reflections with environmental details
feature.dynamic_cubemaps.key_feature_4: Support for both standard and VR rendering modes

feature.effects11.category.lens_desc: Overall lens effect amount handed to the shaders.

feature.effects11.category.proceduralsun: Sun disk size, edge softness and glow.

feature.effects11.category.rays_desc: Screen-space light shafts streaming from the sun, or from a moon at night.

This allows for advanced post-processing effects and visual enhancements using DirectX 11 Effect (.fx) files.

feature.exp_height_fog.apply_vanilla_fad: Applies vanilla fade brightness to exponential height fog.
feature.exp_height_fog.dir_inscattering_:
Controls the asymmetry of inscattering via the Henyey-Greenstein phase function.
Positive values produce forward scattering (glow around sun).
Zero is isotropic. Negative values produce back scattering.
feature.exp_height_fog.disable_vanilla_f: Disables the vanilla fog entirely. Only exponential height fog will be applied.
feature.exp_height_fog.distance_haze_fad: Horizontal distance beyond Haze Start Distance over which haze smoothly reaches its maximum opacity, in game units.
feature.exp_height_fog.distance_haze_max: Adds haze at all heights using the fog colors above, while preserving dense height fog. Zero disables distance haze.
feature.exp_height_fog.distance_haze_sta: Horizontal distance from the camera where haze begins, in game units. Independent of height fog Start Distance.
feature.exp_height_fog.mist_drift_speed_: Manual drift speed, or the speed at full outdoor wind strength. Changing speed only affects future movement. Zero freezes the pattern; pausing also pauses animation.
feature.exp_height_fog.mist_follow_wind_: Uses the current outdoor wind direction and strength, smoothing changes over one second. Calm wind stops drift. Interiors retain manual drift. Wind changes movement, not density.
feature.exp_height_fog.mist_movement_off: Total distance the mist pattern has drifted this session.
feature.exp_height_fog.mist_range_toolti: Coverage and outer fade distance. It does not change pocket density.
feature.exp_height_fog.mist_size_tooltip: Scale of the mist pattern. Density is adjusted to keep each pocket's optical thickness.
feature.exp_height_fog.mist_strength_too: Scales weather-driven opacity across one mist pocket, independently of Mist Range. Higher values make pockets thicker when you enter them. Zero removes the added mists.
feature.exp_height_fog.mists_description: Adds drifting 3D mist pockets nearby, using the existing volumetric grid and lighting. Strength follows the active fog: clear weather stays restrained. This is an artistic addition to the vanilla match, not an exact match.
feature.exp_height_fog.mists_range_help: Range cannot extend the volumetric grid. Small pockets fade where the grid is too coarse to resolve them. Speed 0 freezes the pattern in the world.
feature.exp_height_fog.mists_requires_vo: Enable Exponential Height Fog and Volumetric Fog to render mists.
feature.exp_height_fog.sample_jitter_mul:
Matches UE's r.VolumetricFog.LightScatteringSampleJitterMultiplier.
Adds per-voxel random offset on top of the Halton sequence.
0 = UE default; nonzero values need stronger temporal filtering.
feature.exp_height_fog.second_fog_layer_:
Adds a second stacked exponential height fog layer with its own base height, density and height falloff.
The two line integrals are summed.
Use it for high-altitude haze above the ground layer or a distinct low-lying ground fog.
feature.exp_height_fog.upsample_jitter_m:
Matches UE's r.VolumetricFog.UpsampleJitterMultiplier.
Jitters the final 3D fog lookup in screen space to hide
low-resolution froxel pixelization. 0 = UE default.
feature.exp_height_fog.use_dynamic_cubem: Use Dynamic Cubemaps for Interior Inscattering
Adds the dynamic environment cubemap color to the fog inscattering in interiors.
feature.exp_height_fog.use_sky_ibl: Use Sky IBL for Exterior Inscattering
feature.exp_height_fog.use_sky_ibl_toolt: Adds the sky IBL color to the fog inscattering in exteriors. Requires the Image Based Lighting feature.
feature.exp_height_fog.use_vanilla_fog_s: Derives fog density, start distance, and colors from the active weather while keeping exponential height falloff. Weather Fog Strength scales density. Replaces vanilla distance fog.
feature.exp_height_fog.volumetric_extinc: Scales fog density when following vanilla fog, including when volumetric fog is off. In manual mode, affects only volumetric fog.
feature.exp_height_fog.volumetric_near_g:
Distance covered by the full-resolution near volume.
A second, quarter-lattice far volume covers the remaining distance up to the Volumetric View Distance.
Smaller values improve near-field resolution; larger values move the low-resolution far volume farther away.
feature.exp_height_fog.volumetric_noise_:
Modulates the volumetric fog density with a 3D value noise field.
Noise Scale: spatial frequency of the fog clumps (0 = disabled).
Noise Threshold: soft cutoff that carves clumps out of the noise.
Noise Velocity: animation drift of the noise field, scaled by time.
Noise Type: Hash is the original field. PCG Quintic uses an integer lattice that stays exact far from the origin.
feature.exponential_height_fog.descripti: Exponential Height Fog adds a realistic fog effect that increases in density with height, enhancing atmospheric depth and immersion in the game environment.
feature.exponential_height_fog.name: Exponential Height Fog
feature.extended_materials.description:
Extended Materials adds advanced material effects including parallax occlusion mapping and complex material blending.
This feature enhances surface detail and depth perception for more realistic textures.
feature.extended_materials.enable_comple: Enables support for the Complex Material specification which makes use of the environment mask. This includes parallax, as well as more realistic metals and specular reflections. May lead to some warped textures on modded content which have an invalid alpha channel in their environment mask.
feature.extended_materials.enable_height: Enables landscape texture blending based on parallax.
feature.extended_materials.enable_legacy: Enables terrain parallax using the alpha channel of each landscape texture. Therefore, all landscape textures must support parallax for this effect to work properly.
feature.extended_materials.enable_parall: Enables parallax on standard meshes made for parallax.
Enables a fix reducing parallax scale on curved and smooth normal triangles.
feature.extended_materials.enable_shadow: Enables cheap soft shadows when using parallax. This applies to all directional and point lights.
feature.extended_materials.name: Extended Materials
feature.extended_translucency.blend_weig: Control the blend weight of the effect applied to the final result.
feature.extended_translucency.default_ma:
Anisotropic translucency will adjust the opacity based on your view angle to the translucent surface.
  - Disabled: No anisotropic translucency, flat alpha.
  - Rim Edge: Naive rim light effect with no physics model, the edge of the geometry is always opaque even its full transparent.
  - Isotropic Fabric: Imaginary fabric weaved from threads in one direction, respect normal map, also works well for layer of glass panels.
  - Anisotropic Fabric: Common fabric weaved from tangent and birnormal direction, ignores normal map.
feature.extended_translucency.descriptio:
Extended Translucency provides realistic rendering of thin fabric and other translucent materials.
This feature supports multiple material models for different types of translucent surfaces.
feature.extended_translucency.key_featur: Multiple translucency material models (rim edge, isotropic/anisotropic fabric)
Realistic fabric translucency with directional light transmission
Per-material override support via NIF extra data
feature.extended_translucency.name: Extended Translucency
feature.extended_translucency.skinned_me: Control if this effect should only apply to skinned mesh. Check this option if you are seeing undesired effects on random objects.
feature.extended_translucency.softness_t: Control the softness of the alpha increase, increase the softness reduce the increased amount of alpha.
feature.extended_translucency.transparen: Translucent material will make the material more opaque on average, which could be different from the intent. Reduce the alpha to counter this effect and increase the dynamic range of the output.

feature.foliage_lighting.foliage_ambient: Amount added to the diffuse indirect ambient response for animated trees.
feature.foliage_lighting.name: Foliage Lighting
feature.fur_shells.body_length_tooltip: Fur length on skin, such as khajiit bodies and heads, in game units.
feature.fur_shells.create_override_toolt: Saves these values as a .json beside the shell texture. Mod Organizer 2 puts the new file in Overwrite, so the texture's mod stays untouched.
feature.fur_shells.description: Grows layered fur on armors and creatures at draw time from the shell textures that fur mesh mods ship, so the layered meshes themselves are no longer needed.
feature.fur_shells.discard_override_tool: Reloads the saved override for this texture, or returns it to the settings above when none is saved.
feature.fur_shells.droop_tooltip: How far the tips sag, in game units.
feature.fur_shells.enabled_tooltip: Draws fur shells on meshes whose texture has a _shell.dds beside it.
feature.fur_shells.fade_tooltip: Shells thin out between these distances and stop past the end.
feature.fur_shells.hide_covered_fur_tool: Skips fur whose roots are covered by clothing, armor or anything else in front of them, so it stops poking through. Works in the world view, not in first person or menus.
feature.fur_shells.inertia_droop_exponen: How much a droopier fur asset swings slower and lags more. 0 ignores droop.
feature.fur_shells.inertia_frequency_too: How fast fur of the reference length and droop swings and settles. Higher is stiffer.
feature.fur_shells.inertia_gain_tooltip: Scales how far the tips lag for a given acceleration, before Inertia Strength. Stylized uses 2, Realistic uses 1.
feature.fur_shells.inertia_length_expone: How much longer fur swings slower and lags more. 0 ignores length; 2 follows a real hair.
feature.fur_shells.inertia_max_bend_tool: The furthest the tips may lag, as a fraction of the fur length.
feature.fur_shells.inertia_preset_toolti: Stylized is the tuned-by-eye look. Realistic uses the physics of a real hair, so short fur barely moves and long fur swings. Custom exposes the spring.
feature.fur_shells.inertia_strength_tool: How far the fur tips lag behind a moving mesh before springing back, so fur trails when the wearer starts, stops or turns. 0 disables inertia.
feature.fur_shells.key_feature_1: Uses the _shell.dds texture next to an armor or creature texture
feature.fur_shells.key_feature_2: Works on any body shape, refit or physics mesh
feature.fur_shells.min_fur_pixels_toolti: Fur thins out as its on-screen height falls below this many pixels and is skipped at zero. 0 disables the cutoff.
feature.fur_shells.name: Fur Shells
feature.fur_shells.overlay_fur_tooltip: Carries RaceMenu overlays such as tattoos, body paint and fur patterns up through the fur, so they color it instead of staying hidden under it. Each overlay in use draws the fur once more.
feature.fur_shells.override_active: This texture uses its own values.
feature.fur_shells.override_enabled_tool: Turn off to stop fur growing on meshes that use this shell texture.
feature.fur_shells.override_inactive: No override yet. This texture follows the settings above.
feature.fur_shells.root_darkening_toolti: Brightness at the root. Tips stay at full brightness.
feature.fur_shells.root_threshold_toolti: Shell texture alpha needed at the root. Lower is denser.
feature.fur_shells.shell_color_tooltip: 0 colors the fur from the armor's own texture, 1 from the shell texture.
feature.fur_shells.shell_count_tooltip: Layers drawn up close. Each one is another lighting pass over the fur.
feature.fur_shells.shell_texture_tooltip: Shell textures drawn this session. If one is missing, bring its armor or creature on screen first.
feature.fur_shells.show_touch_edges_tool: Tints touched fur to show how far a hand or body reaches: red inside the touching shape, magenta along the edge of the affected fur, cyan to yellow as the push grows. For tuning only.
feature.fur_shells.tip_threshold_tooltip: Shell texture alpha needed at the tip. Higher thins the strands toward the end.
feature.fur_shells.touch_strength_toolti: How strongly hands, fingers and bodies press and drag the fur they touch, including fur on your own gear in VR. 0 disables touch.
feature.fur_shells.wet_strength_tooltip: How much rain mats the fur: wet fur thins into clumps, darkens and hangs heavier. Water beads and drips on the outer layer come from Wetness Effects. 0 disables wet fur.
feature.fur_shells.wind_strength_tooltip: How strongly the world wind bends the fur. Fur is only blown outdoors. 0 disables wind.
feature.grass_collision.compression_reco: Lower values keep grass compressed longer after an actor moves away.
feature.grass_collision.description: Enables dynamic grass interactions where grass bends and moves in response to actors walking through it, creating more immersive environmental reactions.
feature.grass_collision.key_feature_1: Real-time grass deformation from actor movement
feature.grass_collision.key_feature_2: Bounded collision processing for nearby actors
feature.grass_collision.key_feature_3: Dynamic tracking of actor positions for grass response
feature.grass_collision.key_feature_5: Seamless integration with existing grass rendering
feature.grass_collision.maximum_compress: Grass taller than this can still bend around actors but will not be vertically compressed.
feature.grass_collision.name: Grass Collision
feature.grass_lighting.brightness_toolti: Darkens the grass textures to look better with the new lighting
feature.grass_lighting.description:
Grass Lighting enhances grass rendering with improved lighting, specularity, and subsurface scattering.
This makes grass appear more natural and responsive to lighting conditions.
feature.grass_lighting.detection_thresho: Threshold for detecting complex grass textures. Lower values are more strict.
feature.grass_lighting.enable_wrapped_li: Enables a softer-looking wrapped lighting model from CS 1.3. Useful for certain non-complex grass textures that look too dark during midday, when the sun is directly overhead.
feature.grass_lighting.far_lod_brightnes: Raise or lower until the most distant LOD grass matches the middle LOD grass in front of it. Requires Grass Optimizations with Far LOD enabled.
feature.grass_lighting.mid_lod_brightnes: Raise or lower until middle-distance LOD grass matches the full-detail grass around it. Requires Grass Optimizations with Middle LOD enabled.
feature.grass_lighting.name: Grass Lighting
feature.grass_lighting.override_complex_: Override the settings set by the grass mesh author. Complex grass authors can define the brightness for their grass meshes. However, some authors may not account for the extra lights available from {brand}. This option will treat their grass settings like non-complex grass. This was the default in Community Shaders < 0.7.0
feature.grass_lighting.sss_tooltip: Subsurface Scattering (SSS) amount. Soft lighting controls how evenly lit an object is. Back lighting illuminates the back face of an object. Combined to model the transport of light through the surface.
feature.grass_optimizations.cost_bias_st: Distance at which Mesh Cost Bias starts taking effect, ramping to full over the same distance again. Nearer than this, all grass types are treated identically no matter how complex. Zero applies the bias everywhere, including right in front of the player.
feature.grass_optimizations.description: Rewrites grass rendering around GPU-driven culling and instancing, consolidating thousands of engine draw calls into a handful of indirect draws and removing hidden grass before it costs anything.
feature.grass_optimizations.edge_fade_st: Percent of the grass render distance at which grass starts fading out. The default of 0.85 fades over the last 15%. A lower value results in a longer, smoother fade out, while a value of 1.0 disables the fade and grass pops out at the render distance.
feature.grass_optimizations.enable_far_l: Swaps the most distant grass to the _LOD1.nif mesh. Grass types without that file reuse their _LOD0.nif, so the far band still gets its own brightness.
feature.grass_optimizations.enable_mesh_: Improves performance by swapping distant grass instances for a simpler LOD mesh, in two bands. Requires an LOD .nif per grass type at meshes\LOD\Grass\<source-mesh-name>_LOD0.nif, plus an optional _LOD1.nif for the far band. Grass with no LOD mesh keeps its full mesh.
feature.grass_optimizations.enable_mid_l: Swaps mid-distance grass to the _LOD0.nif mesh. With this off, grass stays on its full mesh until the far band takes over.
feature.grass_optimizations.enabled_tool: Use GPU-driven grass culling and instanced draws. When disabled, grass renders through the vanilla path and all other settings are ignored.
feature.grass_optimizations.far_lod_pixe: Instances whose on-screen radius is below this but above Min Pixel Size swap to the _LOD1.nif mesh. Values above the Middle LOD Pixel Size are clamped to it, since the far band is always the more distant of the two.
feature.grass_optimizations.full_detail_: Instances whose on-screen radius is above this render at full density. Below it, density is increasingly thinned down to Minimum Density at Min Pixel Size. Increasing this setting improves performance by removing closer grass.
feature.grass_optimizations.invisible_fa: Skip drawing grass whose transparency is below this threshold. Grass with a fade value of zero is completely invisible and thus is removed early for performance reasons.
feature.grass_optimizations.key_feature_: Consolidates per-shape grass draws into one instanced indirect draw per mesh tier per grass type
GPU compute culling of individual instances by frustum, distance and projected size
Hi-Z occlusion culling skips grass hidden behind objects before the vertex shader runs
Configurable render distance beyond the vanilla INI cap with density scaling
Optional mesh-swap LOD and simplified shading for distant grass
feature.grass_optimizations.mesh_cost_bi: Culls or removes grass meshes based on their complexity (performance impact). At 0, removal is identical between all grass types regardless of complexity. At 1, heavier and more complex meshes are culled 2-6x sooner than simple ones. Only applies beyond the Cost Bias Start Distance, so nearby grass is never thinned.
feature.grass_optimizations.mesh_lod_ban: The range of on-screen sizes over which a random amount of meshes are swapped out before completely transitioning to the next LOD. Applies to both transitions. A wider range results in a smoother transition.
feature.grass_optimizations.mid_lod_pixe: Instances whose on-screen radius is below this but above the Far LOD Pixel Size swap to the _LOD0.nif mesh.
feature.grass_optimizations.min_density_: The percentage of grass that remains at the smallest (Min Pixel Size) LOD level before culling.
feature.grass_optimizations.min_pixel_si: Individual grass instances that visibly take up less space on the screen than this are dropped entirely. Higher values improve performance by removing far-away grass instances sooner.
feature.grass_optimizations.name: Grass Optimizations
feature.grass_optimizations.occlusion_bi: How far behind an occluder grass must sit before Occlusion Culling removes it. Raise this if grass disappears around the edges of rocks and hills, lower it to reclaim more performance. Has no effect unless Occlusion Culling is enabled.
feature.grass_optimizations.occlusion_cu: Skips grass hidden behind rocks, buildings and NPCs. Depending on how much grass is not visible, this may cost more than its benefits. If you see grass flickering when moving, try disabling this. Terrain such as hills is not treated as an occluder when Terrain Blending is enabled, which reduces the benefit.
feature.grass_optimizations.render_dista: Max grass render distance in units. 0 = use the game's INI cap (fGrassStartFadeDistance + fGrassFadeRange). Any grass beyond the vanilla range or this range will be removed.
feature.grass_optimizations.simple_shadi: Grass instances smaller than this size on screen will skip barely visible detail including contact shadows, specular highlights, and other complex grass visual elements. Zero disables this feature.
feature.hair_specular.description: Provides better hair shading with realistic specular highlights and tangent-based light interaction for more lifelike hair appearance.
feature.hair_specular.enable_self_shadow:
Enables screen-space self-shadowing for hair.
Marschner hair model might have overly bright transmission without self-shadowing.
feature.hair_specular.enable_tangent_shi:
Enables the use of a tangent shift texture to vary specular highlights across hair strands.
Result may vary based on the hair model used.
feature.hair_specular.glossiness_tooltip:
Controls the glossiness of the hair.
Glossiness in Kajiya-Kay mode maps to the specular exponent.
In Marschner mode, it controls the roughness of the hair surface.
feature.hair_specular.hair_mode_tooltip:
Select the hair shading model to use.
Kajiya-Kay is an empirical model that simulates hair specular highlights.
Marschner is a more physically-based model that simulates hair light interaction.
Both models are anisotropic and support tangent-based shading.
Without self-shadowing, Marschner may look overly bright because of transmission.
feature.hair_specular.key_feature_2: Enhanced hair glossiness and saturation controls
feature.hair_specular.key_feature_3: Separate specular and diffuse lighting multipliers
feature.hair_specular.key_feature_4: Tangent shift texture support for varied hair highlights
feature.hair_specular.name: Hair Specular
feature.hdr_display.advanced_tooltip_ena: Enable Windows HDR instead of forcing it here.
feature.hdr_display.advanced_tooltip_for: Force enable HDR even without detection (not recommended).
feature.hdr_display.auto_hdr_peak_cap: Effects11 AutoHDR is active: peak brightness is capped at %u nits.
feature.hdr_display.capable_display_wind: HDR Capable Display (Windows HDR is off)
Your monitor supports HDR, but Windows HDR is currently disabled.
Enable HDR in Windows Display Settings to allow auto-detection.
feature.hdr_display.description: Real High Dynamic Range output for HDR displays.
feature.hdr_display.display_reports_max_: Reported by OS/driver (DXGI MaxLuminance), not a direct meter reading.
It may be EDID metadata and can differ from real highlight peak output.
Treat this as a starting point and tune Peak Brightness as needed.
feature.hdr_display.enable_hdr_tooltip: Enable HDR output. Matches vanilla visuals with extended dynamic range.
feature.hdr_display.enable_hdr_tooltip_n: HDR display not detected. Use Advanced button to override.
feature.hdr_display.enable_hdr_tooltip_w: Monitor supports HDR but Windows HDR is off. Enable HDR in Windows Display Settings, then restart the game.
feature.hdr_display.enabled_without_dete: HDR is enabled but no HDR display was detected.
feature.hdr_display.exclusive_fullscreen: HDR is not compatible with Exclusive Fullscreen and may not work correctly. Switch to Borderless Windowed mode for proper HDR support.
feature.hdr_display.force_enable_hdr_con: Only proceed if you have an HDR-capable display that was not detected correctly.
feature.hdr_display.force_enable_hdr_det: HDR was not detected on your monitor.
feature.hdr_display.force_enable_hdr_sdr: The game will look VERY WRONG on an SDR (standard) display.
feature.hdr_display.key_feature_1: HDR10 output support (10-bit) with upgraded HDR buffers (16-Bit), and fully unclamped rendering pipeline for true HDR values.
feature.hdr_display.key_feature_2: HDR-aware tonemapping based on Skyrim's ISHDR path (Reinhard/Hejl-Burgess-Dawson), preserving the vanilla look while improving highlight handling on HDR displays.
feature.hdr_display.key_feature_3: Configurable paper white and peak brightness.
feature.hdr_display.name: HDR Display
feature.hdr_display.paper_white_tooltip_: How bright SDR white appears on your HDR display.
203 nits is the ITU BT.2408 reference. Increase for a brighter image.
feature.hdr_display.peak_brightness_tool: Maximum brightness your display can produce.
Set to match your display's actual peak brightness.
feature.hdr_display.ui_brightness_multip: UI brightness = Paper White x this multiplier in HDR mode.
1.00x = UI renders at Paper White brightness. Higher values make UI brighter relative to scene content.
Note: Main menu and loading screens always render at Paper White brightness.
feature.ibl.dalc_amount_tooltip:
Blends the IBL brightness toward the game's vanilla ambient (DALC) level.
0 = no matching (pure IBL brightness), 1 = fully matched to vanilla ambient.
feature.ibl.dalc_mode_tooltip:
Luminance Ratio: Scalar ratio from overall luminance (loses DALC color tint).
Color Ratio: Per-channel ratio (preserves DALC color tint).
DALC + Sky: Uses vanilla ambient as base, sky IBL on top. Skylighting only affects sky.
DALC + Sky (Directional): Same, but Skylighting also dims vanilla ambient per-direction.
feature.ibl.description: Replaces the game's ambient lighting with physically-based IBL derived from cubemap spherical harmonics.
feature.ibl.enable_ibl_tooltip: Toggle IBL. When enabled, ambient lighting is derived from cubemap spherical harmonics instead of the vanilla system.
feature.ibl.enable_in_loading_screen_too: Enables IBL during loading screens and the main menu.
feature.ibl.enable_in_world_map_tooltip: Enables IBL while the world map is open.
feature.ibl.env_ibl_saturation_tooltip:
Color saturation of the environment IBL.
Lower values produce more neutral ambient light; higher values produce more vivid color.
feature.ibl.env_ibl_scale_tooltip:
Intensity multiplier for the environment IBL (from Dynamic Cubemaps).
Controls how strongly the surrounding environment contributes to ambient lighting.
feature.ibl.fog_mix_tooltip:
Blends the fog color toward the IBL ambient color.
0 = vanilla fog, 1 = fog fully tinted by IBL.
feature.ibl.key_feature_1: Projects environment and sky cubemaps into spherical harmonics (SH) for irradiance
feature.ibl.key_feature_2: Dual IBL sources: environment cubemap (Dynamic Cubemaps) and Skyrim's native sky reflections cubemap
feature.ibl.key_feature_3: DALC brightness matching to keep IBL consistent with the game's ambient light levels
feature.ibl.key_feature_4: Configurable per-source intensity, saturation, fog mixing, and per-weather overrides
feature.ibl.key_feature_5: Static IBL fallback textures for out-of-world objects (e.g. inventory items)
feature.ibl.name: Image Based Lighting
feature.ibl.preserve_fog_luminance_toolt:
When Fog Mix is active, rescales the IBL-tinted fog to keep the original fog brightness.
Prevents fog from becoming too bright or too dark.
feature.ibl.sky_ibl_saturation_tooltip:
Color saturation of the sky IBL.
Lower values produce more neutral ambient light; higher values produce more vivid color.
feature.ibl.sky_ibl_scale_tooltip:
Intensity multiplier for the sky IBL (from the game's native reflections cubemap).
Controls how strongly the sky contributes to ambient lighting.
feature.ibl.use_static_ibl: Use Static IBL For Out-of-World Objects
feature.ibl.use_static_ibl_tooltip: Uses pre-baked static IBL cubemap textures for objects rendered outside the game world (e.g. inventory items, loading screens).
feature.interior_sun.description: Allows for the sun and moon to cast light and shadows into interior spaces.
feature.interior_sun.force_double_sided_: Disables backface culling during sun shadowmap rendering in interiors. Will prevent most light leaking through unmasked/unprepared interiors at a small performance cost.
feature.interior_sun.interior_shadow_dis: Sets the distance shadows are rendered at in interiors. Lower values provide higher quality shadows and improved performance but may cause distant interior spaces to light up incorrectly.
feature.interior_sun.key_feature_1: Functions only for explicitly enabled interiors
feature.interior_sun.key_feature_2: Utilizes existing sun, moon, and weather systems
feature.interior_sun.key_feature_3: Includes an option to force double-sided rendering for unprepared interiors
feature.interior_sun.key_feature_4: Fixes geometry culling issues that cause light leakage
feature.interior_sun.name: Interior Sun

feature.light_editor.choose_attach_type: Choose an attach type (Model, FormID, or EditorID).
feature.light_editor.confirm_delete_entr: Delete this light entry from the Light Placer JSON?
feature.light_editor.delete_entry_toolti:
Delete this light entry from the Light Placer JSON.
If it is the only light in its entry, the whole models/formIDs entry is removed too.
feature.light_editor.filter_update_faile: Filter update failed â see log
feature.light_editor.light_already_in_en: This light already exists in this entry.
feature.light_editor.log_mode_tooltip: Extend slider ranges and use a logarithmic scale.
feature.light_editor.no_attached_bulbs: This mesh has no attached Light Placer bulbs.
feature.light_editor.no_base_record: Picked object has no base record.
feature.light_editor.no_cell_editor_id: This mesh's cell has no EditorID.
feature.light_editor.no_filter_list_entr: This mesh has no whitelist or blacklist entries.
feature.light_editor.no_model_path: No model path on this object.
feature.light_editor.no_source_plugin: No source plugin on this object.
feature.light_editor.object_no_model_pat: This object has no model path.
feature.light_editor.object_no_source_pl: This object has no source plugin for a FormID entry.
feature.light_editor.pick_mesh_prompt: Click a mesh to attach a light... (right-click / ESC to cancel)
feature.light_editor.reload_lp_tooltip: Reload all Light Placer JSON configs in-game (reloadlp).
feature.light_editor.save_as_separate_en:
Fork this bulb into a new whitelist entry for %s with the current edits, and blacklist it from the shared entry so the edits apply only to this reference.
Reload LP to apply.
feature.light_editor.save_color_tooltip:
Include color when saving to Light Placer.
When unchecked, the light falls back to the LIGH form color.
feature.light_editor.save_to_lp_match_to:
Matching entry found in %s.
Save current settings to the Light Placer JSON.
feature.light_editor.save_to_lp_no_match:
No matching entry found in %s.
Saving will fail.
feature.light_editor.select_mesh_tooltip: Click a mesh in the world to attach a new bulb, edit an existing bulb, or whitelist/blacklist this reference.
feature.light_editor.select_mesh_vr_unsu: Mesh picking is not supported in VR.
feature.light_editor.shadows_only_toolti: Only show lights with HemiShadow or OmniShadow flags.
feature.light_editor.toggle_all_lp_light: Toggle all Light Placer lights on/off (tlp 0).
feature.light_editor.toggle_light_lp_too: Toggle this reference's LP-placed lights on/off (tlp 0).
feature.light_limit_fix.allow_immediate_: Allow Immediate Draw for New Lights

Allow a light just added to the active pool to render its shadow map this frame.
Prevents a one-frame shadow-map gap when new lights enter view.
feature.light_limit_fix.atlas_full_capac: Fits ~%u lights at full %u px detail

A full-detail tile is one vanilla shadow map, sized by the game's
own shadow resolution setting. Lights beyond this count still cast
shadows, at reduced detail, ordered by priority. Raise Atlas
Resolution to keep more at full detail; raising the game's shadow
resolution makes each tile sharper but fewer of them fit.
feature.light_limit_fix.atlas_reallocs_t:
Each reallocation is a light changing resolution class,
which discards its cached shadow and forces a redraw.
A fast-growing number means the scene is fighting the
class hysteresis; a slow one means the cache is holding.
feature.light_limit_fix.atlas_resolution:
Size of the shared shadow texture. Bigger sizes keep more lights
at full shadow detail but use more video memory. Takes effect
after restarting the game.
feature.light_limit_fix.avg_redraws_tool: Rolling average over the last %d frames.
feature.light_limit_fix.billboard_bright: Intensity multiplier for billboard (single-quad) emitters such as candle flames.
feature.light_limit_fix.billboard_radius: Radius multiplier for billboard emitters. Larger = light reaches further.
feature.light_limit_fix.budget_from_form: Edit the Redraw Budget formula in the Advanced section below.
feature.light_limit_fix.budget_mode_form:
Formula: user-editable math expression for per-frame budget.
Default expression matches Intellightent's original behaviour
(1 ms outdoors, 2 ms indoors). Edit the expression in the
Advanced section below.

Caveat: adaptive expressions referencing `frametime` tend to
ping-pong because rendering shadows raises frametime, removing
the headroom that allowed the budget. Stick to static or
slowly-varying inputs (`isinterior`, `frametarget`).
feature.light_limit_fix.budget_mode_manu:
Manual (default): fixed per-frame GPU time budget for shadow re-renders.
Predictable; doesn't oscillate. Adjust the slider to trade FPS for shadow quality.
feature.light_limit_fix.caster_cull_angu:
Skip a shadow caster when its on-screen size from your viewpoint
(bound radius / distance to camera) is below this. A close caster
filling the view is kept even if small; a distant one in a corner
is dropped even if large. Large speedup in cluttered interiors.
0 disables. Useful range is small -- Balanced/Performance presets
use 0.008/0.012. Ctrl+Click the slider to type an exact value.
Lower it if distant shadows look like they pop in.
feature.light_limit_fix.changed_tooltip:
Time since this light last changed role (shadow / converted / out).
Sort this column to bring just-changed lights to the top.
feature.light_limit_fix.clear_all_toolti:
Reset every debug override:
  - clear suppression
  - clear shadow / convert pins
  - clear solo
Returns the table to scheduler-auto behaviour.
feature.light_limit_fix.contact_shadow_l: Ray length toward each light near the camera. Farther away it grows with depth so the shadow keeps its size on screen. Longer = more screen-space reach with coarser detail.
feature.light_limit_fix.contact_shadow_m: View-space depth at which contact shadows fade to zero steps. Avoids paying for shadows on distant surfaces where they don't read.

Raymarch steps at zero depth, packed toward the shaded point. A ray spends only as many steps as its length on screen allows, and above four steps rays that never approach an occluder are rejected early.

Skip contact shadows for CLUSTERED lights whose normalized distance falloff `1 - (lightDist/radius)^2` at the pixel is below this threshold. Strict lights are always raymarched regardless of this threshold. Higher = larger perf win, may drop subtle shadows from weak lights at their reach edge.
feature.light_limit_fix.contact_shadow_t: Assumed thickness of every surface. A ray passing further behind a surface than this goes around it instead of being shadowed. Higher values treat surfaces as thicker and shadow more behind them.
feature.light_limit_fix.conv_reason_exce: Reason: excess -- ranked below the shadow-caster budget.
feature.light_limit_fix.conv_reason_frus: Reason: frustum/distance-culled -- off-screen, or beyond the shadow-cull distance.
feature.light_limit_fix.conv_reason_lod: Reason: LOD-faded -- past the light's LOD fade-out distance.
feature.light_limit_fix.conv_reason_misc: Reason: rejected by the engine visibility test.
feature.light_limit_fix.conv_reason_port: Reason: portal-culled -- the light's room isn't reachable through the visible portal graph.
feature.light_limit_fix.convert_excess_t:
Shadow lights that exceed the active shadow caster limit are demoted to
normal (unshadowed) lights so they still contribute diffuse and specular
lighting at no shadow-map cost. Lights that fail culling are dropped entirely.
Requires a game restart to change.
feature.light_limit_fix.converted_shadow:
Extra pool slots for lights converted to normal (unshadowed) mode.
Increase if Convert Excess Lights drops lights you expect to see.
feature.light_limit_fix.demand_tile_cap_:
Gives a light the GPU measures as lit on screen far less than the
best-lit light a small shadow tile, so blocked lights stop taking large tiles.
feature.light_limit_fix.description: Light Limit Fix removes the vanilla game's 4-light limit, allowing unlimited dynamic lights in scenes. It also extends shadow support to all point and spot lights.
feature.light_limit_fix.dump_atlas_toolt:
Save the shadow atlas depth texture (DDS) plus a
per-slot tile manifest (JSON) to
Data/SKSE/Plugins/CommunityShaders/Captures.
Written on the next shadow pass.
feature.light_limit_fix.enable_contact_s: All point lights (strict and clustered, except simple lights) cast short screen-space shadows. Performance impact.
feature.light_limit_fix.enable_lights_vi: Enables visualization of the light limit
feature.light_limit_fix.enable_particle_: Also cast contact shadows from particle lights. Larger performance impact in fire/magic-heavy scenes.
Significantly improves performance by not rendering empty textures. Only disable if you are encountering issues.
Adds particle lights to the player light level so that NPCs detect them for stealth and gameplay.
Master toggle for the particle-light feature.
Merges vertices which are close enough to each other to improve performance.
feature.light_limit_fix.enable_shadow_li:
Extends Skyrim's hard limit of 4 simultaneous shadow-casting lights.
Intelligently selects which lights cast shadows each frame based on
distance, intensity, and a configurable priority formula.

Based on Intellightent by meh321.
https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/172423

Restart required to take effect in either direction. The boot-time
patches (extended atlas slices, depth buffer creation loop, color-mask
pass replacement) cannot be safely reversed at runtime -- vanilla
shadow scheduling crashes when run on top of them. Toggle and restart.
feature.light_limit_fix.exterior_shadow_:
Distance (game units) past which exterior shadows are culled
(fShadowDistance:Display). Also drives the directional sun cascade
range, so higher values soften distant outdoor shadow transitions
at a GPU cost. Applies live; persisted on Save Settings.
feature.light_limit_fix.flicker_tooltip:
How a cached shadow follows a flickering light:
Live: the shadow origin follows the light and the cached depth is
copied unmoved, which leaves a small mismatch near occluders.
Pinned: the shadow origin stays at the bake pose, so the shadow
does not move with the flame.
Warped: the cached depth is reprojected to the live origin on the
GPU, so the shadow moves with the flame.
P / W in the shadow light table marks lights using Pinned / Warped.
feature.light_limit_fix.force_portal_str:

Force room-visibility (portal-strict) culling on hemisphere
(single dome projection) shadow casters. Recommended on --
behaves like the omni case under portal culling.
Requires a game restart to change.
Force Portal Strict on Omni Lights

Force room-visibility (portal-strict) culling on omnidirectional
(dual dome projection, aka dual-paraboloid) shadow casters.
Recommended on -- tightens room visibility culling for full-sphere
shadow lights without side effects.
Requires a game restart to change.
Force Portal Strict on Spot Lights

Force room-visibility (portal-strict) culling on perspective
(frustum/spot) shadow casters. Off by default: the cone test
rejects spots whose origin sits behind a portal even when their
beam sweeps into a visible room, which drops culled-but-visible
spots entirely.
Enable only for debugging.
Requires a game restart to change.

feature.light_limit_fix.redraw_budget_ms:
Per-frame GPU time budget for shadow re-renders (milliseconds).
Lights whose estimated render cost exceeds the remaining budget are deferred.
The first eligible light always renders regardless of budget (starvation prevention).

Reference points (typical; depends on the scene):
  1-2 ms: Intellightent's original (1 outdoors, 2 indoors)
  5 ms : about one light per frame; the rest refresh every few frames
  7 ms : default, about two lights per frame at ~3 ms each
  12 ms: about four lights per frame at ~3 ms each
  16 ms: full 60 fps frame; shadows can saturate the frame here
  32 ms: extreme, only useful for very high light counts on fast GPUs

Higher = more shadow lights redraw per frame, fewer stale shadow maps,
at the cost of frametime. The Budget verdict in the Active Casters
section shows whether the current setting has headroom to spare.
feature.light_limit_fix.redraw_due_gate_: Stop Early Once Nothing Is Due

Stops spending the redraw budget once every light with an actually-
stale shadow (moved, changed, or never drawn) has been redrawn this
frame, instead of always using the full budget on whichever light is
next in priority order even when its shadow is already correct.
Reduces GPU cost the most in scenes with many lights but few that are
actually changing (e.g. a lit interior with the player standing still).
Worst-case staleness stays bounded by Shadow Staleness Ceiling above.

Shadow Mask: R=directional soft shadow, G=directional detailed shadow.

Shadow Light Count: Heatmap of shadow-casting point/spot lights per pixel (blue=0, red=8+).
Use to gauge shadow density; high counts indicate expensive shadow sampling.

Point Light Shadow Factor: Brightness shows the darkest shadow value from any point/spot
light. White=fully lit, black=fully shadowed. Shows where PCF/PCSS filtering is active.

Unshadowed Point Lights: Heatmap of point/spot lights without shadow maps (blue=0, red=8+).
High values where lights are bright indicate where the shadow slot limit is costing quality.

Shadow Caster Density: Custom Turbo ranges show how heavily shadow slots are used.
  Cool (Turbo 0.0-0.3): 1-4 shadow lights per pixel.
  Warm (Turbo 0.3-0.8): 5 to ShadowMapSlots lights (dynamic range).
  Bright red: overflow - a light wanted a shadow slot but none was available.

Shadow Slot Index Color: Assigns each shadow-map slot a unique high-contrast hue
(golden-ratio sequence) so you can identify which slot is casting the primary shadow.
First valid shadow light index per pixel is shown. Bright red = slot overflow.

Light Type Visualization: RGB channels encode shadow light types per pixel.
  R = spot/frustum lights (ShadowParam.x == 0).
  G = hemisphere lights (single dome projection; ShadowParam.x == 1).
  B = omnidirectional lights (full dome projection; ShadowParam.x == 2).
  Dark grey = unshadowed lights only (no shadow maps assigned).
  Bright red = overflow (slot capacity exceeded).
Intensity scales with count (up to 4); channels blend for mixed-type pixels.

Minimum ISO reached: overexposed. Close the aperture or shorten the shutter time.

How much to affect purity compression and hue shift as Peak Luminance increases.
A value of 0.0 will keep the purity compression and hue shift behavior the same for SDR and HDR.
A value of 1.0 will preserve more purity as peak luminance increases

feature.post_processing.open_drt.how_qui: How quickly above the Contrast High Pivot the effect begins.
feature.post_processing.open_drt.hue_con:
Hue Contrast compresses hue angle towards the primary at the bottom end and expands the hue angle towards the secondary as intensity increases.
It also increases purity as it compresses, and decreases purity as it expands.
This leads to a nice creatively controllable simulation of this effect from per-channel tonescales.
For OpenDRT we only keep the red hue angle control since it is the most useful.

Hue contrast range control: determines where over the intensity range the hue contrast affects.
Higher values place the crossover point higher in the intensity range.
feature.post_processing.open_drt.hue_shi:
Hue Shift CMY adds hue distortion to the cyan magenta and yellow secondary hue angles as intensity decreases.
This module allows some very minimal adjustments of secondary hue angles as a creative tool.

Hue Shift RGB adds hue distortion to the red green and blue primary hue angles as intensity increases.
By default OpenDRT will compress purity in a straight line in RGB/Chromaticity space.
This can lead to perceived hue shifts due to the Abney Effect, for example a pure blue will perceptually shift towards purple as it desaturates.
To compensate for this, and to use as a creative tool, this module allows creative control over the path that red green and blue hue angles take as their purity is compressed.
feature.post_processing.open_drt.limit_t:
Limit the intensity range affected by the Creative Whitepoint.
At 0.0, the entire intensity range is affected. As the limit is decreased, more of midtones and shadows are kept neutral.
It can be creatively desireable to keep midtones more neutral while shifting highlights warmer for example.

Limit the strength of blue purity compression as intensity increases.
Can be helpful to keep some color in high intensity pure blue light sources.
Use with caution as this can cause gradient disruptions.

Limit the strength of purity compression as intensity decreases, for all hue angles.
A higher value will compress purity less in midtones and shadows.

Limit the strength of purity compression as intensity decreases, for reds.
A higher value will compress purity less in midtones and shadows.

Limit the strength of purity compression as intensity decreases, for all greens.
A higher value will compress purity less in midtones and shadows.

feature.post_processing.open_drt.opendrt:
OpenDRT includes a simple surround compensation model.
DCI cinema presets use dark surround. Rec.1886 uses dim surround. And sRGB Display uses bright surround.
This functionality should provide a better perceptual match between viewing environments.
feature.post_processing.open_drt.peak_di:

In SDR, the max value stays pinned at 1.0. In HDR, this is overridden by HDR Display Peak Brightness.
feature.post_processing.open_drt.post_br:
Post Brilliance scales the intensity of more pure stimuli after purity compression hue shifts have been applied.
With the OpenDRT algorithm it is possible to get high intensity high purity values going out of the top of the display-referred gamut volume,
which can cause discontinuities in gradients, especially on the RGB primaries.
This module can help compensate for this.
feature.post_processing.open_drt.pre_ton:
Pre-tonescale scene-linear offset.
If 0.0, scene-linear 0.0 maps to display-linear 0.0 through the tonescale system.
Many camera imaging pipelines apply a negative offset to set the average of shadow grain at 0.0.
A positive Offset can be desireable to compensate for this and increase detail in shadows, in addition to being aesthetically desireable.
Offset should NOT be a negative number (Looking at you ACES 1.x)
feature.post_processing.open_drt.purity_:
Purity Softclip increases tonality and smoothness in extremely pure input values
that can not be adequately compressed into the display-referred gamut volume.
The algorithm is tuned for common camera observer colorimetry sources.
feature.post_processing.open_drt.quadrat:
Quadratic toe compression.
Strongly compresses deep shadows. Helpful to have some amount to smooth the transition into display minimum.
Higher values with a strong positive Offset also valid. Similar to common camera DRT tonescale strategies.

feature.post_processing.physical_glare.a:
Aperture f-number (e.g. F2.8). Smaller = larger aperture = wider diffraction spikes.
Physically: aperture radius = 1 / f-number.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.d: Physically based glare from aperture diffraction and ocular scattering. FFT convolution with a wavelength-dependent PSF, dual eye/lens modes, wavefront aberrations, and wide-gamut chromatic dispersion.

Dust particles on lens element surfaces.
Produces scattered haze via Babinet's principle.

Dynamic range compression exponent (paper Table 3.9: 0.45).
Lower = wider/softer glare, higher = concentrated near light source.
Increase if glare looks too blurry/spreads too far.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.f:
Fresnel phase at aperture edge (radians). Paper eq 2.12: e^(i*pi/(lambda*z) * r^2).
Higher = more Fresnel rings. 0 = pure Fraunhofer (no rings).
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.h: How fast the glare adapts to brightness changes.
How fast the tear film fluctuates (blink refresh rate ~0.3Hz, breakup ~2-5Hz).
How opaque each scratch is. Higher = more visible streaks.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.l: Length of eyelashes relative to aperture radius.
Length of scratches relative to aperture size.
Lens: camera lens polygon starburst. Pupil: circular human eye aperture.

Lens fiber radial phase grating.
Creates many thin, sharp radial star spikes.
Higher count = more spikes (typical human eye: 20-80). 0 = disabled.

Lens suture lines: Y-shaped junctions where lens fiber cells meet.
3 = young eye (anterior Y + posterior inverted Y = 6 spikes).
More branches = older/more complex lens. 0 = disabled.

Linear scratches on lens element surfaces.
Each scratch produces a perpendicular streak in the glare.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.m:
Micro-serrations on aperture blade edges (manufacturing imperfections).
Makes star spikes slightly fuzzy/irregular. 0 = perfect edges.

Multiplier on wavelength-dependent UV scaling (paper section 2.3: lambda/575nm).
1.0 = physically correct. Higher = more rainbow spread. 0 = monochrome.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.n: Number of angular harmonics. More = more spikes, finer detail.
Number of aperture blades. Controls starburst pattern.
Number of bumps per blade edge. Higher = finer serrations.

Number of radial lens gratings (paper section 2.4: Ritschel uses 200).
Produces lenticular halo via edge diffraction.

Number of scatter particles in lens/vitreous (Ritschel: 750).
Produces ciliary corona needle pattern via Babinet's principle.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.o: Opacity of lens gratings. Higher = stronger lenticular halo.

Opacity of scatter particles in pupil mode (paper section 2.4).
0 = transparent (no scatter), 1 = fully opaque.
Opacity of suture lines. Higher = stronger star spikes.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.p: Per-channel brightness threshold for glare extraction in EV100 (0 EV100 = 0.125 linear luminance).
Phase shift strength per fiber. Higher = brighter spikes.
Pixel width of each suture line. Thinner = sharper spikes.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.r: Radius of each dust particle in pixels.
Radius of each particle in pixels.

Random variation in fiber spacing and strength.
0 = perfectly regular (even spikes).
1 = maximally irregular (natural look).
Resolution of the FFT convolution. Higher = sharper starburst but more expensive.
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.s:
Scale of the glare kernel size on screen.
1.0 = default. Smaller = more concentrated glare.
Does not affect aperture physics.

Seidel spherical aberration (r^4 wavefront error).
Models lens curvature: outer rays focus at a different point
than central rays, producing concentric ring structure in the
PSF and softer glare edges. Physical range: 0-50.
Simulate eyelash occlusion for streak effects (paper section 3.1).

Simulates tear film irregularities on the cornea surface.
Produces flickering, sharp, irregular star spikes.
0 = disabled (static PSF).
Streak curvature via UV bending (paper fig 3.7: sin(x) vertical offset).
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.t:
Threshold to remove low-level FFT noise from the PSF.
Paper default: 0.001. Higher = cleaner glare wings.
Total number of eyelash hairs (upper + lower).
feature.post_processing.physical_glare.z:
Zero-padding per side to prevent FFT wrap-around.
0.25 = paper default (50% effective resolution).
0.1  = 80% effective (recommended for high-res).
0.0  = 100% (maximum sharpness, may wrap at edges).
Lower = sharper glare on high-res screens.

feature.reverse_z.description:
Renders the scene with an inverted, floating-point depth buffer so that depth precision is spread evenly across the view distance instead of being concentrated near the camera. This removes most distant z-fighting on terrain, LOD and large meshes.

The main depth buffer is reallocated at a wider format, which costs additional video memory and depth bandwidth. Changing this setting requires a game restart.

feature.reverse_z.key_feature_4: Costs extra video memory and depth bandwidth

feature.screen_space_gi.description: Screen Space Global Illumination adds realistic indirect lighting and ambient occlusion to the game. This technique simulates how light bounces off surfaces to illuminate other objects naturally.
feature.screen_space_gi.enabled_tooltip: Enable Screen Space Global Illumination. When disabled, all other settings are ignored.
feature.screen_space_gi.geometry_weight_: Higher value makes the blur more sensitive to differences in geometry.
feature.screen_space_gi.hq_specular_il_t: An experimental specular GI that is more accurate but requires more samples. Won't be blurred.
feature.screen_space_gi.il_radius_toolti: A larger radius produces wider IL.
feature.screen_space_gi.indirect_lightin: Pending restart: needs AO + GI Resources.
feature.screen_space_gi.max_frame_accumu: How many past frames to accumulate results with. Higher values are less noisy but potentially cause ghosting.
feature.screen_space_gi.min_screen_radiu: The minimum screen-space effect radius as proportion of display width, to prevent far field AO being too small.
feature.screen_space_gi.movement_disoccl:
If a pixel has moved too far from the last frame, its radiance will not be carried to this frame.
Lower values are stricter.
feature.screen_space_gi.name: Screen Space GI
feature.screen_space_gi.profile_ao_gi_to: Enables full indirect lighting at the cost of more video memory. Requires a game restart to change.
feature.screen_space_gi.profile_ao_only_: Uses less video memory but disables indirect lighting. Requires a game restart to change.
feature.screen_space_gi.slices_tooltip:
How many directions do the samples take.
Controls noise.
feature.screen_space_gi.steps_per_slice_:
How many samples does it take in one direction.
Controls accuracy of lighting, and noise when effect radius is large.
feature.screen_space_gi.thickness_toolti: How thick the occluders are. Only affects AO.
feature.screen_space_gi.vanilla_ssao_too: Enable Skyrim's built-in SSAO. Usually disabled when using SSGI to avoid double-darkening.
Vanilla SSAO is not supported in VR.
feature.screen_space_gi.vr_stereo_reproj: Reprojects Eye 0 (left)'s diffuse GI into Eye 1 (right) and skips the Eye 1 march where it can, reducing GPU cost. Requires HQ Specular IL off (specular is view-dependent). Disoccluded pixels are marched natively instead.
feature.screen_space_gi.vr_warning: Warning: In VR, this feature may have visual artifacts and can have a significant performance impact due to the nature of screen space effects.
feature.screen_space_shadows.bilinear_th: Depth threshold for edge detection during bilinear interpolation. Higher values smooth more aggressively across edges.
feature.screen_space_shadows.description:
Screen Space Shadows enhances shadow quality by adding detailed contact shadows and improving shadow accuracy.
This technique adds fine-detail shadows that traditional shadow mapping might miss.
feature.screen_space_shadows.enable_tool: Enable screen-space contact shadows from the sun/moon direction.
feature.screen_space_shadows.fov_screen_:
Uses the active Upscaling FOV mask for Screen Space Shadows.
When enabled, full-quality SSS is computed inside the FOV mask and fades to no SSS outside it.
The mask center follows the active DLSS/upscaler foveation subrect.
The mask area, horizontal scale, and per-eye offsets are taken from Upscaling; SSS has no separate FOV size.
feature.screen_space_shadows.fov_unavail: Enable Foveated Render in the Upscaling settings; it takes effect after a restart.
Foveated Render currently covers the full frame, so there is nothing to foveate.
Requires DLSS, which this GPU or driver does not support.
Requires the DLSS or FSR upscaler: set Upscaling's method to one of them.
Foveated Render is enabled but needs a game restart to take effect.
Requires Screen Space Shadows to be enabled.
feature.screen_space_shadows.name: Screen Space Shadows
feature.screen_space_shadows.sample_coun: Multiplier for shadow ray sample count. Higher values increase shadow reach at the cost of performance. Adapts to render resolution.
feature.screen_space_shadows.shadow_cont: Contrast boost for the shadow transition. Higher values produce harder shadow edges.
feature.screen_space_shadows.surface_thi: Assumed thickness of surfaces for shadow detection. Lower values produce thinner, more precise shadows.
feature.screen_space_shadows.vr_stereo_s:
Off: each eye computes shadows independently (may mismatch between eyes).
On: both eyes compute, then reconcile (matches between eyes, highest cost).
