feature.sky_sync.moon_light_source_toolt: Select which moon casts shadows during the night.
feature.sky_sync.name: Sky Sync
feature.sky_sync.shadow_transition_durat: How long (in game-time units) the shadow direction takes to fade between sources. 300 = ~15 seconds at timescale 20.
feature.sky_sync.sun_path_tooltip: Choose the trajectory the sun takes across the sky.
feature.sky_sync.use_alternate_sun_path_: Calculate sun position based on time of day and season instead of vanilla movement.
feature.skylighting.capture_interval_too: Minimum frames between captures while stationary. Higher values reduce work but slow lighting refresh. Requires Reduced Update Frequency.
feature.skylighting.description: Simulates realistic ambient lighting by calculating sky occlusion and directional lighting, providing more accurate and natural illumination in outdoor environments.
feature.skylighting.diffuse_min_visibili: Sets the minimum diffuse skylight visibility. Lower values darken surfaces sheltered from the sky.
feature.skylighting.enabled_tooltip: Enables skylighting captures and probe updates. Turning it back on rebuilds the lighting history.
feature.skylighting.incremental_tooltip: Lower counts reduce update work but slow field refresh. Capped at the selected grid depth; requires Incremental Probe Updates.
feature.skylighting.incremental_updates_: Updates part of the probe grid per capture while stationary. Movement and rebuilds update the full grid.
feature.skylighting.key_feature_1: Sky occlusion calculation for ambient lighting
feature.skylighting.key_feature_2: Directional skylighting based on environment geometry
feature.skylighting.key_feature_3: Enhanced ambient lighting for outdoor scenes
feature.skylighting.key_feature_4: Support for varying sky illumination intensities
feature.skylighting.max_zenith_tooltip: Smaller angles focus shadows more directly overhead. Use Rebuild Skylighting after changing this value.
feature.skylighting.name: Skylighting
feature.skylighting.performance_options_: Start with update frequency, then slice count and grid size to trade lighting responsiveness and detail for speed.
feature.skylighting.probe_field_width_de: Wider fields cover more ground but reduce spatial detail and increase capture cost. Changes rebuild probe history.
feature.skylighting.probe_grid_tooltip: Smaller grids reduce update work and memory use but lower spatial detail. Changing the grid rebuilds probe history.
feature.skylighting.probe_interval_toolt: Minimum frames between full-grid updates; fresh captures can delay updates further. Requires Reduced Update Frequency with Incremental Probe Updates off.
feature.skylighting.rebuild_tooltip: Clears and rebuilds skylighting history. Use after changing Max Zenith Angle to apply it throughout the field.
feature.skylighting.reduced_frequency_to: Allows longer capture and probe intervals while stationary. Increase an interval above 1 for savings; movement and rebuilds bypass the delays.
feature.skylighting.specular_min_visibil: Sets the minimum sky contribution to reflections. Lower values darken reflections in sheltered areas.
feature.sss.mean_free_path_color_tooltip: Controls how far light goes into the subsurface in the red, green, and blue channel. It is scaled by the Mean Free Path Distance.
feature.sss.mean_free_path_distance_tool: Controls the distance that Mean Free Path Color goes into subsurface.
feature.sss.post_scatter_tooltip: Divide out albedo, blur the irradiance, multiply albedo back. Preserves texture detail.
feature.sss.pre_and_post_scatter_tooltip: Split albedo across the blur using sqrt(albedo) on each side. A physically motivated middle ground.
feature.sss.pre_scatter_tooltip: Blur the lit color directly. Fastest, but blurs albedo texture detail along with lighting.
feature.subsurface_scattering.descriptio:
Subsurface Scattering simulates light penetration through translucent materials like skin, creating more realistic character lighting.
This technique makes organic materials appear more lifelike and natural.
feature.subsurface_scattering.name: Subsurface Scattering
feature.terrain_blending.description: Provides seamless blending between terrain and objects, eliminating harsh transitions where objects meet the ground for more natural-looking landscapes.
feature.terrain_blending.enable_tooltip: Enable seamless blending between terrain and objects.
feature.terrain_blending.key_feature_2: Advanced depth buffer manipulation for smooth integration
feature.terrain_blending.key_feature_3: Support for alternative terrain rendering modes
feature.terrain_blending.key_feature_4: Multi-pass rendering optimization for complex scenes
feature.terrain_blending.key_feature_5: Enhanced visual continuity in landscape interactions
feature.terrain_blending.name: Terrain Blending
feature.terrain_helper.description: Provides enhanced terrain material support for terrain mods that require additional texture slots and parallax mapping capabilities.
feature.terrain_helper.key_feature_1: Extended texture slot support for terrain materials
feature.terrain_helper.key_feature_2: Parallax mapping integration for terrain textures
feature.terrain_helper.key_feature_3: Automatic terrain material detection and setup
feature.terrain_helper.key_feature_5: Compatibility layer for terrain enhancement mods
feature.terrain_helper.name: Terrain Helper
feature.terrain_shadows.description: Adds realistic shadow casting from terrain features using heightmap data to create accurate terrain shadows that enhance depth perception and visual realism.
feature.terrain_shadows.key_feature_2: Dynamic shadow updates based on sun position
feature.terrain_shadows.name: Terrain Shadows
feature.terrain_variation.always_enabled: Terrain Variation is always enabled when installed. To turn it off, use Disable at Boot.
feature.terrain_variation.apply_to_lod_t:
Applies the tiling fix to LOD terrain objects.
This helps reduce the visible tiling effect on distant terrain.
feature.terrain_variation.description:
Terrain Variation reduces the repeating pattern effect on terrain textures.
This technique creates more natural-looking terrain by adding variation to texture sampling.
feature.terrain_variation.enable_mesh_su:
Applies the tiling fix to meshes that use landscape textures, such as dirt cliffs and mountain slabs.
Alpha tested meshes like foliage and decals are never affected.
feature.terrain_variation.name: Terrain Variation
feature.true_pbr.micro_shadow_strength_t: How strongly ambient occlusion darkens direct light.
feature.true_pbr.micro_shadows_tooltip: Occludes direct light with the material's ambient occlusion map, adding contact shadowing to surface detail such as seams, rivets and fabric weave.
feature.true_pbr.name: True PBR
feature.upscaling.description: Advanced upscaling and frame generation technologies for improved performance
feature.upscaling.dlss_model_preset_tool:
Choose which DLSS AI model preset to use.
Default lets the NVIDIA runtime choose for each upscale mode.
Current defaults are K for DLAA, Quality, and Balanced; M for Performance; and L for Ultra Performance.
An explicit preset overrides every upscale mode.
feature.upscaling.dlss_resolution_warnin: Warning: Requested resolution %.0f x %.0f exceeds maximum supported resolution %d x %d for DLSS.
feature.upscaling.dlss_will_not_function: DLSS will not function. Lower your resolution or select a different upscaling method.
feature.upscaling.dlssg_frame_multiplier: How many total frames are shown per rendered frame. Higher values generate more frames.
feature.upscaling.enable_sharpening_tool:
Applies RCAS sharpening to the DLSS output.
Off by default; DLSS already resolves a sharp image.
feature.upscaling.ffx_dll_table_title: AMD FidelityFX DLLs (click to open folder)
feature.upscaling.fg_dlssg_unavailable: DLSS-G is unavailable this session; AMD FSR is in use.
feature.upscaling.fg_fsr_frame_limit_too:
Caps FSR's total FPS to the display refresh rate.
When generation pauses, caps rendered FPS instead.
feature.upscaling.fg_not_loaded: Frame generation is not loaded. Check the setup above and restart.
feature.upscaling.fg_warn_fidelityfx_mis: Warning: FidelityFX DLLs are not loaded
feature.upscaling.fg_warn_refresh_rate: Enable the option above to use frame generation on displays below 120 Hz.
feature.upscaling.force_enable_frame_gen:
Bypass the high-refresh-rate monitor check so Frame Generation can run on lower-Hz
displays. Useful for laptops and older monitors at the cost of less headroom for the
generated frames.
feature.upscaling.foveated_active: Active: foveated subrect upscaling is enabled (skipped in the main and loading menus / on preflight failure).
feature.upscaling.foveated_blend_dither_: Noise-dithered fade — more natural-looking than feather at large subrects.
feature.upscaling.foveated_blend_feather: Smoothstep fade over N pixels at the boundary. Hides the seam. Falloff Curve reshapes the ramp.
feature.upscaling.foveated_blend_hard_co: Sharp seam at the subrect boundary. Lowest cost.
feature.upscaling.foveated_dlss_mode_def: Per-eye isolation: 5 copies per frame, 2 DLSS evaluates. All presets.
feature.upscaling.foveated_dlss_mode_fas: Viewport offset: 1 snapshot, 2 mask clears, 2 DLSS evaluates. Presets J/K unavailable.
feature.upscaling.foveated_dlss_mode_fsr: Not used by FSR -- applies only when DLSS is the selected upscaler.
feature.upscaling.foveated_dlss_mode_too:
Default — highest quality. Each eye gets its own isolated copy of color/depth/motion
vectors so DLSS can't sample across the stereo midline. 5 copies per eye per frame.
All DLSS presets supported. Best for screenshots or when Faster shows edge artifacts.

Faster — lower overhead. DLSS reads directly from the frame buffer using a viewport
offset instead of isolating each eye. 1 snapshot + 2 mask clears per frame.
DLSS may sample 1-2 pixels from the neighboring eye near the stereo center — usually
invisible in motion. Presets J and K are incompatible and auto-clamp to L.
feature.upscaling.foveated_falloff_curve: Controls how the transition distributes the fade. 1.00 is balanced; lower values carry the upscaled result farther into the band, higher values hold the periphery longer.
feature.upscaling.foveated_mask_shape_to: Oval rounds the blended edge, so the subrect corners keep the stretched periphery instead of the upscaled image. The upscaler still processes the full rectangle either way.
feature.upscaling.foveated_overview: Foveated subrect upscaling: only the user-selected region gets full DLSS/FSR upscaling, the periphery is cheaply stretched. Significant upscaler cost reduction at the cost of peripheral sharpness. VR only.
feature.upscaling.foveated_periphery_aa_: Blends the stretched periphery with motion-reprojected history to reduce flicker.
feature.upscaling.foveated_periphery_too:
The area outside your selected subrect is filled cheaply rather than running
the selected upscaler. These settings control how that cheap fill looks and
whether it flickers.

Stretch method: how pixels outside the subrect are reconstructed from the lower-res
render buffer. Does not affect the upscaled subrect region at all.

Periphery AA: reduces temporal flicker in the stretched area using motion-compensated
history blending. Independent of the upscaled subrect.

Edge Blend: controls how the upscaled subrect edge meets the stretched periphery.
Hard Copy leaves a sharp seam; Feather/Dither soften it. Edge Shape selects a
rectangle or oval composite.
feature.upscaling.foveated_screenshot_su: Screenshot has its own subrect; align them only if you want pixel-matched captures.
feature.upscaling.foveated_shared_panel_: Quality and Sharpness are on the main Upscaling panel — changes there apply to foveated rendering too. DLSS Preset also applies there when DLSS is the selected upscaler.
feature.upscaling.foveated_smoothing_too: Lower = more temporal history (smoother but may ghost). Higher = more responsive.
feature.upscaling.foveated_standing_by: Standing by: only active while the Upscaling Method is DLSS or FSR. Inactive right now.
feature.upscaling.foveated_standing_by_f: Standing by: region is Full Eye (no crop) -- shrink it in Subrect Region below to see savings.
feature.upscaling.foveated_stretch_bilin: Bilinear: smooth upscale of the render buffer. Looks soft but clean.
feature.upscaling.foveated_stretch_gauss: Gaussian: blurs the periphery further into soft focus. Good default for foveated use.
feature.upscaling.foveated_stretch_point: Point: cheapest, visibly pixelated. Good for benchmarking foveated savings.
feature.upscaling.foveated_subrect_regio: Drag in the preview below to select the region that gets full upscaling. The rest is cheaply stretched — saves significant upscaling cost.
feature.upscaling.foveated_visualize_reg:
Diagnostic: tint the cheap-stretched periphery red so the upscaled
subrect (un-tinted) pops visually in-game. Lets you confirm at a glance where
the selected upscaler is actually running vs where the cheap stretch is filling.
No perf impact; runtime toggle, no restart needed. Also shows briefly whenever
you drag-resize the region below, even with this off.
feature.upscaling.foveated_vr_only: VR only -- flat has no equivalent lens-driven periphery quality cliff to exploit.
feature.upscaling.fps_limit_tooltip_2: Start about 2-3 FPS below refresh rate (e.g. 117 for 120 Hz).
feature.upscaling.frame_generation_in_me: Keeps frame generation active while game menus are open.
May feel smoother, but increases menu input latency.
feature.upscaling.frame_generation_toolt:
Enable frame generation for smoother motion. Uses AMD FSR unless NVIDIA DLSS-G is selected and available.
Requires windowed mode.
feature.upscaling.frame_limit_vrr: Limit FPS to display refresh rate
feature.upscaling.fsr4_failed_fallback: Runtime FSR4 failed this session -- using FSR 3.1.
feature.upscaling.fsr4_runtime_failed_fa: Runtime upscaler DLL failed this session -- using host FSR 3.1.
feature.upscaling.low_latency_boost_tool: Keeps GPU clocks higher to avoid latency spikes at low GPU load.
Useful if frametime jumps; costs extra power and heat.
feature.upscaling.low_latency_mode_toolt: Cuts input delay by syncing CPU work closer to the GPU.
Can reduce max FPS a little, but usually feels more responsive.
feature.upscaling.method_locked_opencomp: Locked to None while OpenComposite has %s=true.
feature.upscaling.name: Upscaling
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.allow: Loads a 310.8.x or 310.9.x runtime that is not one of the builds checked in game. Its colour channels may be wrong; turn this off if the picture looks tinted.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.categ: Scales Neural Rendering's tone edit per material: 0 leaves a material's brightness untouched, 1 is the normal edit, and 2 doubles it. Materials the deferred buffer does not label are unaffected.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.crop_: Calibration failed: frame generation on, Neural Rendering not running, or no timing data.
Largest crop that is still cheap: %.0f%%

Measures how Neural Rendering's GPU time falls as the crop shrinks, over about half a minute, and finds the largest crop that is still about as cheap as the smallest. Turn frame generation off first; it skews the timing.
Timing was unsteady between passes; run it again.
How much margin the crop keeps around the tracked character. Padded keeps the normal margin; Tight evaluates the character's own outline with no margin, for checking what the crop covers.
Grows the crop to also cover the next most prominent characters while it stays under half the view, so a group is evaluated together. Off tracks one character.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.cross: Fill Gaps From The Other Eye

Where a reused eye could not take its own earlier gain (a surface that just came into view), it takes the gain the other eye's model frame computed this frame for the same surface. Costs one extra sample per such pixel and no extra model time.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.descr: One display-referred NR proxy pass at eye render resolution, composed back into scene-linear HDR before DLSS/FSR and frame-generation capture. Requires an NR-capable NVIDIA GPU and a validated 310.8 or 310.9 runtime build.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.dialo: Evaluates Neural Rendering only while a dialogue is open, and leaves the frame's rendering untouched the rest of the time. The pass stays initialized, so opening a dialogue resumes it without a rebuild.
Full frame evaluates the whole view during dialogue instead of the character's crop. It needs Limit to Tracked Actor on; Same as normal follows that setting.
In dialogue, apply Neural Rendering to

What Neural Rendering applies to while a dialogue is open. Choosing a scope keeps the by-material lane bound the whole time, at a cost of about 0.04 ms, so entering and leaving dialogue never rebuilds Neural Rendering.
Changes only what Neural Rendering does while a dialogue is open. The default changes nothing: the normal frame and dialogue both follow the settings above.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.edge_: Blends each material's strength into its neighbours over this many pixels; 0 keeps a hard boundary between materials.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.eye_m: How the two eyes are evaluated. Parallel eyes runs each eye's model at once, the second on its own queue: the same image as separate eyes and about 1 ms faster (about 2 ms with Follow Foveation). Side by side evaluates both eyes as one image on a single instance: about 3 ms faster than separate eyes, with a small difference between the halves. Alternate eyes runs one eye's model per frame and reuses its gain on the other: about 3.5 ms faster than separate eyes, but it can mismatch the eyes where the reuse fails. Separate eyes runs one after the other and is the baseline to compare against. Side by side needs Developer Mode. The Performance profile selects Alternate eyes.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.mater: Choose the materials Neural Rendering is applied to, using the labels the deferred pass writes. All selected is the normal behaviour. It changes where the effect shows, not how much GPU time it costs, and needs the deferred pass. Fine-Tune Strengths sets partial amounts.
Each swatch is the colour that material is drawn in. A material that is off keeps its normal pixels.
Strength: 0 at the left, 1 at the right

Tints each pixel by the material the deferred pass labelled it, so a character the classification mislabels is visible. The filter picks which materials show; the mode picks the category's colour or a colour ramp of the strength the by-material selection gives that pixel, read at the pixel without Edge Softness. Needs the deferred pass; unlabelled pixels follow Everything Else.
Neural Rendering by material is unavailable this session, so the whole frame is processed. Check the log; restarting the game retries.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.mirro: Mirror Left Eye To Both Eyes
Feeds the left eye's inputs to both eyes, to check that the two eyes get the same result. The right eye's picture is wrong while this is on.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.model: Weights the upsampled brightness change by how similar the pixels' brightness is, so it follows edges instead of blurring across them.

This runtime ships two networks. Original is the network of the 310.8 runtime. Newest costs less GPU time but changes the picture, so compare faces and hair before keeping it. The change recreates the model.

Runs the model at a fraction of the eye size and carries only its brightness change back to the full image. 0.75 saves about 8% of the model's GPU time and 0.5 about 16%, with a loss of fine detail. It needs Developer Mode and does not apply with Alternate eyes.
With Side by side or a Model Scale below 1, also evaluates each eye alone at full size every frame so a verify capture can compare the two. Roughly doubles the model's GPU time.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.regio: With Foveation on, evaluates only the foveated region, narrowed to the tracked character's crop when that is set, so the periphery keeps its pre-Neural-Rendering content. The upscaler already replaces that periphery with the cheap stretched view.

Restricts Neural Rendering to a crop around the most prominent visible character, the one covering the most of the view with the centre favoured, and leaves the rest of the frame at pre-NR quality. Costs less GPU time when a character is on screen.

Draws the evaluated crop: a green outline in the game frame and the same rectangle over the preview below. Only meaningful with Limit to Tracked Actor on, and it draws nothing while no character is tracked, since the whole frame is evaluated then.
Crop preview appears once Neural Rendering runs a frame.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.runti: Replace it with a validated 310.8 or 310.9 build of that file.
Neural Rendering runtime builds (click to open folder)
Loading this build because developer mode or the unverified-build option is on; its output is unverified.
Neural Rendering runtime: %s %s is a validated build.
Which nvngx_dlssnr.dll to load: the file in the Streamline folder, or one kept in a subfolder of it. Switching unloads the running one and loads the other, and each build is checked on its own.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.skip_: An eye the model skipped runs again two frames after its last run. Notify the model doubles the motion and the frame time it is given, so both frames are covered; Reset the eye's history drops what it accumulated instead.
feature.upscaling.neural_rendering.use_a: NVIDIA's built-in automatic mask. On is the normal setting; turning it off with no mask supplied is an untested configuration.
feature.upscaling.perfmode_active_note: Render-at-upscaled-resolution is active: Method and Upscale Preset changes only take effect after a game restart. Sharpness / model preset / Reflex remain live.
feature.upscaling.prefer_fsr_frame_gen_t:
Selects NVIDIA DLSS-G instead of AMD FSR on supported hardware.
Leave off to use AMD FSR.
feature.upscaling.reflex_not_available: Reflex is not available. Ensure sl.reflex.dll is present and restart.
feature.upscaling.reflex_via_dx12: Reflex is running via DX12 (DLSS Frame Generation active).
feature.upscaling.render_at_upscale_res_: No effect at Native AA (1x): renders at full resolution; raise the Upscale Preset to engage.
Render-at-upscaled-resolution requires DLSS or FSR. Switch upscaler Method to activate.

On by default. The engine pipeline allocates render targets at the upscaled-render
resolution instead of the HMD display resolution; the upscaler (DLSS or FSR) writes
its output to a private DisplayRes texture. Substantial VRAM and bandwidth savings,
especially at high HMD resolutions.

Locked to the Upscale Preset selected at launch: changing the preset (or this
toggle) takes effect after a game restart. At Native AA (1.0x) there is no
render-res reduction, so the lock stays off and preset changes apply live.

Requires DLSS or FSR. Sharpness / model preset / Reflex remain live.
feature.upscaling.sl_dll_table_title: NVIDIA Streamline DLLs (click to open folder)
feature.upscaling.streamline_logging_too: Verbosity of the NVIDIA Streamline backend logs. Useful for debugging issues with DLSS / DLSS-G.
feature.upscaling.upscale_preset_ignored: The Upscale Preset is ignored while VR Render Scale is set. Move it back to Auto to use the preset again (restart required).
feature.upscaling.use_fps_limit_tooltip_: Uses Reflex's internal FPS cap for steadier frametimes.
Can lower latency versus uncapped rendering.
feature.upscaling.use_markers_to_optimiz: Uses frame markers for tighter Reflex timing.
Try On first; turn Off if it causes stutter on your setup.
feature.upscaling.vr_intermediates_not_c: VR intermediates not yet created (enter game world)
feature.upscaling.vr_render_scale_toolti:
Renders the game at a percentage of your headset's resolution, then
upscales it with DLSS or FSR. Auto follows the Upscale Preset.
Takes effect after restarting the game.
feature.vanilla_fresnel.description: Add realistic environmental reflections to vanilla materials.
feature.vanilla_fresnel.enable_ggx_on_gr: Enable Phong to GGX on Grass
feature.vanilla_fresnel.key_feature_1: Add environmental reflections to all materials
feature.vanilla_fresnel.key_feature_3: Optionally turn vanilla phong specular into GGX
feature.vanilla_fresnel.key_feature_4: Optionally turn static cubemaps into dynamic reflections
feature.vanilla_fresnel.name: Vanilla Fresnel
feature.volumetric_lighting.description:
Volumetric Lighting creates realistic light scattering effects through fog, dust, and atmospheric particles.
This adds dramatic god rays and atmospheric depth to both interior and exterior environments.
feature.volumetric_lighting.enable_exter: Volumetric god-rays / fog scattering in exterior cells.
feature.volumetric_lighting.enable_inter: Volumetric god-rays / fog scattering in interior cells.
feature.volumetric_lighting.name: Volumetric Lighting
feature.volumetric_shadows.description:
Volumetric Shadows provides downsampled VSM shadow maps for use by effects like particles and decals.
This improves shadow quality on transparent objects with minimal performance impact.
feature.volumetric_shadows.name: Volumetric Shadows
feature.vr.controls_help: VR controller bindings. Click Rebind, then hold the new button combo.
feature.vr.depth_culling_exteriors: Enable Depth Buffer Culling in Exteriors
feature.vr.depth_culling_exteriors_toolt: Improves performance in exteriors, recommended ON.
feature.vr.depth_culling_interiors: Enable Depth Buffer Culling in Interiors
feature.vr.depth_culling_interiors_toolt: Improves performance in interiors, recommended ON.
feature.vr.description: Provides VR-specific optimizations and enhancements for {brand}, improving performance and visual quality in virtual reality environments.
feature.vr.foveated_hard_cutoff_tooltip:
Hard-skip SSR outside the center region instead of a feathered falloff.
Cheaper, but the transition edge may be visible. Default off (feathered).
feature.vr.foveated_requires_dlss: Requires Foveated DLSS to be active:
feature.vr.foveated_ssr_raymarching_tool:
Reduces screen-space reflection raymarching toward the periphery, using the
active Foveated DLSS region. Central reflections stay full quality; peripheral
pixels fall back to the cubemap / water reflection. VR only.
feature.vr.key_feature_1: Depth buffer culling optimization for VR performance
feature.vr.key_feature_2: ImGuiVRHelper-driven in-headset menu, overlay, and controller input
feature.vr.key_feature_3: Customizable controller button mappings via the helper bindings table
feature.vr.key_feature_4: Stereo reprojection and depth-aware blend consistency
feature.vr.key_feature_6: Enhanced VR compatibility with SteamVR and OpenComposite
feature.vr.min_occludee_box_extent_toolt: Minimum bounding box dimensions for object occlusion culling. Lower values improve performance but may result in visual artifacts.
feature.vr.name: VR
feature.vr.near_clip.fog_constraint_reas: Dynamic Near Clip disables vanilla fog so its depth probe is not confused by nearby fog geometry. Enable Exponential Height Fog for atmospheric fog instead.
feature.vr.near_clip.fog_warning: Enabling this option disables vanilla fog. Please enable Exponential Height Fog instead.
feature.vr.near_clip.help: Distances use Skyrim units. Both eyes share the smaller required near distance. The central depth probe cannot see transparent surfaces or geometry already clipped between samples.
feature.vr.reproject_debug_view_tooltip:
Back-Check/Blend Weight/Edge Detection auto-enable Stereo Blend; setting back to Off restores it.

Off: Normal rendering
Coverage: SSS/SSGI reprojection coverage (black = disoccluded, marched natively)
Back-Check: Round-trip reprojection validation
Blend Weight: Heatmap of bilateral blend intensity
Edge Detection: Highlights depth discontinuities
feature.vr.stereo_blend_color_threshold_:
Minimum luminance difference between eyes to trigger blending.
Set to 0 to blend everywhere. Higher = more selective.
Default: 0.02
feature.vr.stereo_blend_depth_sigma_tool:
Depth sensitivity for the bilateral weight.
Lower values are stricter -- only blend when depths match very closely.
Higher values allow blending across slight depth differences.
Default: 0.01
feature.vr.stereo_blend_dev_mode: Developer mode: no screen-space effects active.
feature.vr.stereo_blend_enable_tooltip:
Post-composite depth-aware bilateral blend between eyes.
Reduces stereo inconsistencies from screen-space effects (SSGI, SSR, etc.).
Each pixel is reprojected to the other eye; blending is applied only where
depth agrees (same surface). Full-screen pass in VR.
feature.vr.stereo_blend_max_factor_toolt:
Maximum blend strength between the two eyes.
Higher values reduce screen-space effect flicker but destroy stereo depth.
Keep below ~0.15 to preserve 3D parallax.
Default: 0.1
feature.vr.vr_perf_reproject_tooltip: Shares eye 0's shading with eye 1 where valid, cutting VR GPU cost. Detailed tuning is in the Stereo tab.
feature.vr_stereo.classify_with_depth_hi:
Classifies from the nearer of the depth pre-pass and last frame's final depth, so surfaces the pre-pass skips, such as alpha-tested rocks and road edges, are no longer culled in the right eye.
Debug only: turning this off reintroduces the missing-geometry bug.
feature.vr_stereo.directional_occlusion_:
Catches silhouette edges a plain depth-match check misses.
Fires when Eye 0 depth is less than this fraction of Eye 1 depth (e.g. 0.9 = Eye 0 more than 10% closer).
Higher = more aggressive. 0 = disabled.
feature.vr_stereo.enable_stereo_reprojec:
Reprojects Eye 0 (left) pixels into Eye 1 (right) using depth and motion data,
skipping redundant full shading where the views overlap.
Reduces GPU cost in VR by shading each pixel fewer times per frame.
feature.vr_stereo.full_blend_distance_to: Geometry closer than this distance (game units) is excluded from culling and rendered natively in both eyes. 0 = disabled.
feature.vr_stereo.reclassify_after_repai:
Re-runs the pixel classification on the finished depth so Screen Space GI reprojection sees the restored objects.
Debug only; runs only when that is on.
feature.vr_stereo.repair_from_eye0_depth:
Restores objects the depth pre-pass skips, such as alpha-tested rocks and road edges, in the right eye from the left eye's final depth.
Debug only: turning this off reintroduces the missing-geometry bug.
feature.water_effects.description:
Water Effects enhances water rendering with realistic caustics and underwater lighting effects.
This feature adds dynamic light patterns and improved water visual quality.

feature.wetness_effects.analysis_not_rai: Rain analysis is available while it is raining.
feature.wetness_effects.chance_tooltip: Portion of raindrops that will actually cause splashes and ripples. Higher values increase effect density but have the least performance impact.
feature.wetness_effects.character_coat_i: Controls the independent water-reflection strength on skin, clothing and armor. Dynamic Cubemaps supplies environmental reflections; direct lights and the ambient fallback work without it.
feature.wetness_effects.character_dry_ti: How long broad retained character sheen takes to fade after global weather wetness falls. Cover immediately suppresses localized beads, impacts, and rivulets; shelter does not start a separate per-character dry timer.
feature.wetness_effects.character_rain_a: Multiplier for character-drop density and arrival rate. Reduce it for low wetness or raise it for saturated surfaces.
feature.wetness_effects.character_rain_s: Three reflective water layers on compatible opaque skin, clothing and armor: tiny settled beads, fresh arriving drops, and long flowing rivulets. feature.wetness_effects.character_wet_sh: Adds a clear wet sheen to eligible skin, clothing and armor from retained surface water; localized beads and rivulets remain stronger.

feature.wetness_effects.description: Adds weather-driven environmental wetness plus model-attached water drops and trails on characters.
feature.wetness_effects.enable_ripples_t: Enables circular ripples on puddles, and to a less extent other wet surfaces
feature.wetness_effects.enable_splashes_: Enables small splashes of wetness on dry surfaces.
feature.wetness_effects.enable_vanilla_r: Enable Vanilla Ripples - Controlled by Splashes of Storms
feature.wetness_effects.enable_wetness_t: Enables a wetness effect near water and when it is raining.
feature.wetness_effects.grid_size_toolti: Spatial grid size for raindrop placement (smaller = more grid cells, higher GPU cost)

feature.wetness_effects.hair_wetness_too: Controls the existing uniform rain-wetness response on character hair. It is separate from model-attached drops and trails.
feature.wetness_effects.interior_exterio: If disabled, will only use the exterior value.
feature.wetness_effects.interval_tooltip: How often raindrop effects are checked (lower = more frequent, moderate performance impact)

feature.wetness_effects.precip_calc_tool: Rates use the raindrop chance, grid size, and interval sent to the shader, and are shown in mm/hr.
feature.wetness_effects.puddle_max_angle: How flat a surface needs to be for puddles to form on it.
feature.wetness_effects.puddle_min_wetne: The wetness value at which puddles start to form.
feature.wetness_effects.enable_volumetri: Water collects in depressions of the landscape height map. Stones stick out, edges are darker, and the bottom shows through with a slight distortion. Drying shrinks the pool from the edges to the deepest point. Off uses the original puddles.
feature.wetness_effects.volumetric_puddl: Skylighting is required, so puddles do not form under roofs. While Skylighting is off, the original puddles are used.

feature.wetness_effects.shore_range_tool: The maximum distance from a body of water that Shore Wetness affects
feature.wetness_effects.vanilla_ripples_: Disabling may not take effect until the next weather change.
feature.wetness_effects.weapon_rain_drop: Adds model-attached droplets and a thin wet sheen to equipped weapons. Weapon droplets never slide or form vertical trails, so bows, staves and drawn weapons remain stable at any orientation.
feature.wetness_effects.weather_transiti: How fast wetness appears when raining and how quickly it dries after rain has stopped.
feature.wind.debug_wind_effect_spawn_cou: How many wind effects to spawn
feature.wind.debug_wind_effect_spawn_too: Replaces active impulses with the selected performance-test pattern and enables transient visualization.
feature.wind.debug_wind_effect_worst_cas: Distributes broad, long-lived directional waves across the Near, Mid, and Far fields. This can be much harsher than normal gameplay.
feature.wind.description: Shared ambient, tree, grass, and transient wind controls.
feature.wind.enable_grass_wind_spring_be: Disable broad wind bending while keeping the custom gust-driven flutter active, so flutter can be tested by itself.
feature.wind.enable_grass_wind_spring_to: Adds spring inertia and rebound to the grass wind response. Disable for an immediate response while keeping bend and flutter active.
feature.wind.enable_wind_field_gust_dist: Animates internal gust shapes while the field travels instead of translating a fixed pattern.
feature.wind.grass_transient_bend_streng: Controls bending from dragon wind, shouts, and other wind impulses independently of ambient Bend Strength. Zero disables their bend input without disabling their flutter.
feature.wind.grass_transient_flutter_fre: Sets the rate of the separate impulse flutter oscillation; it does not change ambient gust flutter.
feature.wind.grass_transient_flutter_hal: Time for the extra flutter amplitude to halve after an impulse stops driving it. This does not change the wind event's own duration.
feature.wind.grass_transient_flutter_str: Controls the separate flutter oscillation excited by shouts and impacts. Zero disables it without changing ambient flutter or spring bending.
feature.wind.grass_transient_shared_sett: Maximum Bend Angle, Tip Flexibility, Downward Wind Bend Share, Physical Spring, and overall Flutter Strength are shared with ambient grass wind. Event size, strength, and duration are configured under Wind Effects.
feature.wind.grass_wind_bend_profile_too: Zero leans the whole blade uniformly; one concentrates bending toward the tip.
feature.wind.grass_wind_compression_to_b: Zero uses vertical compression; 100% converts the same downward-wind response into additional directional bending, limited by Maximum Bend Angle.
feature.wind.grass_wind_flutter_amplitud: Multiplies the existing flutter at low, medium, and high local wind without changing its waveform or gust motion.
feature.wind.grass_wind_flutter_frequenc: Scales Skyrim's flutter waveform across the shared broad and turbulent gust structure.
feature.wind.grass_wind_flutter_gust_inf: Controls how strongly local peaks and troughs in the traveling gust field modulate flutter.
feature.wind.grass_wind_flutter_strength: Scales both ambient and transient blade flutter. Use Grass Impulse Flutter in Transients to adjust only the transient contribution.
feature.wind.grass_wind_flutter_wave_sca: Controls the spatial density of traveling flutter waves without changing gust travel distance. Lower values produce broader, more widely spaced waves so nearby grass flutters together; higher values produce smaller, more numerous waves that vary more rapidly across the landscape.
feature.wind.grass_wind_maximum_tilt_too: Limits how far a grass blade can lean from upright.
feature.wind.grass_wind_response_tooltip: Controls how strongly sampled ambient wind velocity bends the grass.
feature.wind.grass_wind_sensitivity_tool: Scales sampled wind speed before evaluating the low, medium, and high flutter response.
feature.wind.grass_wind_spring_damping_t: Below one allows a natural rebound; one is critically damped; above one settles without overshoot.
feature.wind.grass_wind_spring_frequency: Controls how quickly blades react and rebound. Lower values feel heavier; higher values feel stiffer.
feature.wind.grass_wind_spring_memory_to: Estimate for four RGBA16F textures per field: two response textures and two velocity textures.
feature.wind.grass_wind_spring_quality_t: Each field covers a radial quality range. The next range begins where the previous range ends; grass beyond the far range uses Skyrim's vanilla wind.
feature.wind.name: Wind
feature.wind.process_far_range_transient: Processes transient sources in the Far tree and grass spring tiers. Ambient wind and gusts are unaffected.
feature.wind.process_mid_range_transient: Processes transient sources in the Mid tree and grass spring tiers. Ambient wind and gusts are unaffected.
feature.wind.tree_global_override_note: Runtime only. While enabled, every value below overrides the matching response for all trees, including all custom responses loaded from WindSettings JSONs. Disable it to immediately restore each tree's custom or coded-default response.
feature.wind.tree_leaf_base_wind_flutter: Controls the direct leaf animation strength driven by shared base wind. Gust influence adds only local amplitude variation.
feature.wind.tree_mesh_live_note: Changes apply immediately to every loaded instance of the selected mesh. Save writes only changed values to the last-scanned JSON containing that tree.
feature.wind.tree_per_mesh_response_note: Transient, displacement, and model response values are configured per tree in WindSettings JSONs.
feature.wind.tree_response_conflict_warn: Duplicate tree responses found, trees may not behave as intended
feature.wind.tree_wind_gust_scale_toolti: Scales gust variation only for trees. Grass keeps the full shared gust amplitude.
feature.wind.tree_wind_gust_soft_limit_t: Smoothly compresses only the strongest tree gust peaks instead of clipping them. Set to 0 to disable.
feature.wind.tree_wind_test_active_notic: Tree Meshes runtime test conditions currently override wind speed and gust tuning.
feature.wind.tree_wind_test_runtime_note: Runtime only. Disable this override to immediately return control to weather and the Wind Field settings.
feature.wind.trunk_wind_intensity_toolti: Scales Skyrim's vanilla grass motion; ambient tree bending always uses the shared wind field.
feature.wind.visualize_wind_field_toolti: Colors visible world geometry by GPU-sampled ambient gust pressure.
feature.wind.wind_effect.dragon.enabled_: Makes nearby dragon wingbeats, landings, crashes, and shouts disturb shared visual wind consumers.
feature.wind.wind_effect.dragon.name: Dragons
feature.wind.wind_effect.explosions.enab: Adds radial pressure waves for record-backed magic explosions that hit a reference.
feature.wind.wind_effect.explosions.name: Explosive Magic
feature.wind.wind_effect.fus_ro_dah.deca: Controls how quickly pressure fades behind the moving front. Zero removes the extra trailing falloff.
feature.wind.wind_effect.fus_ro_dah.dist: Scales the rank-specific distance the pressure wave can travel.
feature.wind.wind_effect.fus_ro_dah.enab: Adds Unrelenting Force as a directional wave traveling through the shared wind field.
feature.wind.wind_effect.fus_ro_dah.inte: Scales the rank-specific wind velocity added at the moving pressure wave.
feature.wind.wind_effect.fus_ro_dah.name: Fus Ro Dah
feature.wind.wind_effect.fus_ro_dah.spee: Scales how quickly the wavefront travels through the shared wind field.
feature.wind.wind_effect.fus_ro_dah.widt: Scales the moving pressure-front thickness and the soft falloff surrounding its oval core.
feature.wind.wind_effect.heavy_impacts.e: Adds pressure waves for power attacks, giant, dragon, troll, mammoth, Centurion, transformation, and Shield Charge events.
feature.wind.wind_effect.projectile_magi: Automatically adds launch and impact wind to loaded projectile spells, including mod-added magic.
feature.wind.wind_effect.spell_shout.ena: Adds focused transient wind to major shouts and master Destruction spell activations.
feature.wind.wind_effect.storm_call.enab: Adds a radial pressure wave at each exact Storm Call lightning impact.
feature.wind.wind_effect.storm_call.name: Storm Call Strikes
feature.wind.wind_field_advection_respon: Sets gust travel speed at low, medium, and high wind. Values between these points are interpolated; zero wind remains stationary.
feature.wind.wind_field_color_note: The debug color represents normalized ambient gust pressure. Advection controls transport independently from gust amplitude.
feature.wind.wind_field_gust_advection_m: Changes only how quickly gust structures move through world space; it does not increase local air velocity.
feature.wind.wind_field_gust_amplitude_t: Fractional velocity deviation around the mean; 0.35 produces a 0.65x to 1.35x range.
feature.wind.wind_field_gust_coverage_to: Controls how much of the field contains gust regions; lower values create larger calm gaps.
feature.wind.wind_field_gust_crosswind_s: Controls gust length across the wind direction; lower values produce shorter, more compact blobs.
feature.wind.wind_field_gust_edge_softne: Controls the width of the transition between calm gaps and gust regions.
feature.wind.wind_field_gust_scale_toolt: Controls gust thickness along the wind direction.
feature.wind.wind_field_random_direction: Choose and apply a new random fixed direction immediately.
feature.wind.wind_field_readout_tooltip: Weather Wind is the raw ambient input. Local Wind is the canonical sampled velocity magnitude at the camera. Ambient Gust is the normalized field value used to modulate it.
feature.wind.wind_field_transition_durat: A direction change creates a new, fixed-orientation noise field and lerps the old field into it over this period.
feature.wind.wind_field_use_real_directi: Wind Debug: Use Real Wind Direction
Use the current weather wind direction. Disable this to stage and apply a manual field direction.

menu.advanced.active_shaders_tooltip: List of shaders that have been used in recent frames. Enable Shader Blocking above to use hotkeys to cycle through and block shaders for debugging. Shaders not used for ~1 second are removed from this list.
menu.advanced.avg_parallelism_tooltip_1: Average useful concurrency in this workload.
menu.advanced.avg_parallelism_tooltip_2: Roughly the worker count where adding more cores gives diminishing returns.
menu.advanced.avoid_flow_control_tooltip:
Adds D3DCOMPILE_AVOID_FLOW_CONTROL to the shader compiler flags.
Forces fxc to flatten branches into predicated ops rather than emitting dynamic flow control. Often a win for short branch bodies and uniformly-taken branches; usually a loss for long divergent branches that vanilla flow control would skip entirely.
Resets every launch. Toggling this clears the shader cache and triggers a full recompile.
menu.advanced.background_compiler_thread: Number of threads used to compile shaders during gameplay. One or two threads keep the first launch short without stuttering the frame. Startup compilation still uses the compiler thread count above.
menu.advanced.column_completed_tooltip: Time from build start to when this task finished compiling
menu.advanced.column_defines_tooltip: Number of active define permutations for this task
menu.advanced.column_elapsed_tooltip: Wall-clock compile time for this task
menu.advanced.column_frame_pct_tooltip: Percentage of draw calls this frame
menu.advanced.column_priority_tooltip: Estimated compile-cost priority used for scheduling
menu.advanced.column_queue_pct_tooltip: queueWait / (queueWait + elapsed). High values mean this task waited on a busy scheduler rather than the shader itself being slow to compile.
menu.advanced.column_queue_wait_tooltip: Time spent waiting for a free worker before compilation started
menu.advanced.column_source_kb_tooltip: HLSL source file size at compile time
menu.advanced.column_task_key_tooltip: Shader file, class, and active defines
menu.advanced.compile_trace_busy: Wait for the current build to finish before exporting.
menu.advanced.compile_trace_export_faile: Export failed; check OpenShaders.log for details.
menu.advanced.compile_trace_tooltip_1: Writes every compiled task from the current build to a Chrome Trace Event Format JSON file, importable at ui.perfetto.dev or chrome://tracing.
menu.advanced.compile_trace_tooltip_2: A timeline view can distinguish genuine shader compile cost from external CPU contention during the build (e.g. another process stealing cores), which aggregate stats alone cannot localize in time.
menu.advanced.compiler_threads_tooltip: Number of threads used to compile shaders at startup. Defaults to all logical cores minus one for OS headroom (E-cores included). Higher values finish compilation faster but may make the system less responsive.
menu.advanced.compute_tooltip: Replace Compute Shaders. When false, will disable the custom Compute Shaders for the types above. For developers to test whether custom shaders match vanilla behavior.
menu.advanced.content_store_clear_toolti: Deletes every stored shader. Use this if a shader looks wrong after being restored; the next compile rebuilds the store from scratch. Shaders already in the shader cache are kept.
menu.advanced.content_store_limit_toolti: Least recently used shaders are deleted once the store exceeds this. A full build stores about 120 MB, or about 1.1 GB in Developer Mode, so keep several builds' worth if you switch branches.
menu.advanced.content_store_tooltip:
Keeps every compiled shader keyed by its preprocessed source and compiler flags. After a cache wipe, a branch or build switch, or a rollback, shaders already compiled for the same code are restored instead of recompiled.
Costs one preprocess per shader (tens of milliseconds) and disk space in Data/ShaderCache/ContentStore, trimmed to the least recently used. Takes effect for shaders compiled from now on.
menu.advanced.copy_info_tooltip: Copy complete shader information including cache path to clipboard
menu.advanced.developer_mode_via_log_lev: Currently active because Log Level is debug/trace.
menu.advanced.dump_shaders_tooltip: Dump shaders at startup. This should be used only when reversing shaders. Normal users don't need this.
menu.advanced.enable_developer_mode_tool: Unlocks developer-only options and tooling. Also enabled automatically when Log Level is debug or trace. Use at your own risk.
menu.advanced.enable_file_watcher_toolti: Automatically recompile shaders on file change. Intended for development.
menu.advanced.enable_shader_blocking_too: Enables hotkeys to cycle through and block individual shaders for debugging purposes.
menu.advanced.frame_annotations_tooltip: Enable detailed frame annotations for debugging render passes and draw calls.
menu.advanced.half_precision_tooltip:
Adds D3DCOMPILE_PARTIAL_PRECISION to the shader compiler flags.
Lets fxc downgrade unmarked float ops to FP16 where it can prove safety, on top of the existing min16float type hints.
On FP16-capable GPUs (Pascal+ / GCN+ / Skylake+) this can halve register pressure and double ALU throughput, but it can also introduce minor visual differences in shaders that haven't been audited for precision sensitivity.
Toggling this clears the shader cache and triggers a full recompile.
menu.advanced.hide_compilation_hud_vr_to: Suppresses the background-compilation progress overlay for immersion. The blocking foreground-compile warning still shows, since the game is genuinely paused then.
menu.advanced.infinite_core_efficiency_t: How close runtime is to the infinite-core lower bound.
menu.advanced.infinite_core_gap_tooltip_: Defined as 100 * (1 - S / T_p). Lower is better.
menu.advanced.log_level_tooltip: Log level. Trace is most verbose. Default is info. Debug and Trace also enable Developer Mode.
menu.advanced.makespan_tooltip: Observed wall-clock duration for the full shader build.
menu.advanced.parallelism_tooltip_1: Computed lazily from the last completed build.
menu.advanced.parallelism_tooltip_2: Only evaluated when this Statistics section is open.
menu.advanced.pixel_tooltip: Replace Pixel Shaders. When false, will disable the custom Pixel Shaders for the types above. For developers to test whether custom shaders match vanilla behavior.
menu.advanced.press_key_shader_block_nex: Press any key for Shader Block Next...
menu.advanced.press_key_shader_block_pre: Press any key for Shader Block Previous...
menu.advanced.queue_wait_tooltip_1: Time spent waiting in the ready queue before a worker started compilation.
menu.advanced.queue_wait_tooltip_2: Useful for identifying scheduler-induced delay separate from compile cost.
menu.advanced.refraction_scale_tooltip: Scales the heat-shimmer/refraction distortion around fire and other heat sources. 1.0 is unmodified vanilla strength; 0 disables it.
menu.advanced.shader_defines_tooltip: Defines for Shader Compiler. Semicolon ";" separated. Clear with space. Rebuild shaders after making change. Compute Shaders require a restart to recompile.

menu.advanced.work_tooltip_2: This is not CPU time; it is accumulated task elapsed time.
menu.advanced.work_tooltip_3: Equivalent serial time on one worker if overhead stayed the same.

menu.clear_shader_cache_tooltip: Clears the shader cache and disk cache (if enabled). The Shader Cache is the collection of compiled shaders which replace the vanilla shaders at runtime. The Disk Cache is a collection of compiled shaders on disk. Clearing will mean that shaders are recompiled only when the game re-encounters them.
menu.disable_at_boot_desc: Select features to disable at boot. This is the same as deleting a feature.ini file. Restart will be required to reenable.
menu.faq.a1: {brand} is a fork of Community Shaders that ships features the upstream project has not yet released. Both projects are comprehensive graphics enhancement frameworks for Skyrim that provide advanced lighting, materials, and visual effects. They're designed to be modular, letting you enable only the features you want while maintaining good performance. This fork preserves the upstream runtime layout so user settings and themes are compatible.
menu.faq.a2: Each feature can be found in the left sidebar menu. Click on any feature to access its settings. Most features include presets and detailed tooltips to help you understand what each setting does.
menu.faq.a3: Features may fail to load due to hardware incompatibility, missing dependencies, or conflicts with other mods. Check the 'Feature Issues' tab for detailed information about any problematic features.
menu.faq.a4: Failed shaders are usually caused by mixed file versions. Ensure all features are up to date and avoid mixing files from test builds or outdated versions. Please review the 'Feature Issues' tab and/or Wiki for more information. Update your features and remove any obsolete features.
menu.faq.a5: Start by enabling the Performance Overlay to monitor your FPS. Consider disabling expensive features like Screen Space GI or reducing quality settings. The 'Display' tab also includes upscaling options that can improve performance.
menu.faq.a6: No, {brand} (like upstream Community Shaders) is not compatible with ENB. The plugin will automatically disable itself if ENB is detected.
menu.faq.a7: By default, {brand} uses the END key to open this menu. If your keyboard doesn't have an END key or it's not working, you can change it in the General > Keybindings tab. You can also edit the hotkey in the JSON configuration files.
menu.faq.a8: {brand} is open source. Check out the upstream GitHub wiki for contribution guidelines on the shared architecture; open issues and PRs against this repository for fork-specific work, or against upstream Community Shaders for changes that benefit both projects. Whether you're interested in shader programming, C++ development, or documentation, there's always something to contribute.
menu.faq.a9: Yes! {brand} is completely open source and available on GitHub, as is upstream Community Shaders. You can view the source code, report issues, suggest features, and contribute to either project. Both are licensed under GPL, ensuring they remain free and open for everyone. Branding materials and assets (icons, Nexus branding, typography, etc.) are not covered by the GPL Licence. Any included assets may not be used without explicit permission.

ui.smart_clear_cache_desc:
Watches the next second of rendering and clears only the shaders drawing this scene, twice - once now, and once after this menu closes to catch what it was covering. Everything else stays cached.

The cleared shaders recompile in the background as the scene redraws, so expect a brief stutter and some surfaces reverting to their vanilla appearance until it finishes. That is expected - this clears far less than a full wipe, it does not make the recompile invisible.

Keep the broken area visible while it captures. If the problem persists, use a full clear.

bearforj.analyzer.title: Image Analyzer
bearforj.analyzer.how: Close nothing, just stand still: 8 frames of the game picture are read (without the menu) and rated.
bearforj.analyzer.unsupported: This screen format cannot be read (MSAA or unusual HDR format).
bearforj.analyzer.tip_clip: Highlights are clipped (white blobs). Stronger Bearforj tonemap compresses them.
bearforj.analyzer.tip_crush: Shadows are crushed to black. Raise the night lift / soften the tonemap.
bearforj.analyzer.tip_haze: Hazy / washed out. Thinner height fog.
bearforj.analyzer.tip_dark: Underexposed (too dark). Apply lifts it; if still dark it's the weather imagespace / eye adaptation.
bearforj.analyzer.tip_bright: Overexposed (too bright). Apply compresses highlights; if still bright it's the weather imagespace / eye adaptation.
bearforj.analyzer.tip_grey: Colors are grey. Weather/ENB saturation, or a ReShade preset, may be washing them out.
bearforj.analyzer.tip_noise: Noisy image. Use TAA/DLAA/FSR (Upscaling) or raise SSGI/Skylighting quality.
bearforj.analyzer.tip_flicker: Brightness flickers between frames (stand still while analyzing). If it persists: eye adaptation or SSGI temporal settings.

bearforj.conflict.title: Mish Mish is worried
bearforj.conflict.intro: These mods fight with Bearforj. Nothing was turned off - you decide.
bearforj.conflict.enb.what: ENB replaces the same render passes; Bearforj effects, Linear Lighting and particles can break or double up.
bearforj.conflict.enb.fix: Remove ENB (d3d11.dll + enbseries) or don't use Bearforj with it.
bearforj.conflict.reshade.what: ReShade runs after Bearforj; its tonemap / AO / bloom stack on top of ours.
bearforj.conflict.reshade.fix: Turn off ReShade tonemap/AO/bloom, or lower Bearforj tonemap mix.
bearforj.conflict.second_shader_dll.what: A second Community/Bearforj Shaders DLL is installed; both hook the same shaders.
bearforj.conflict.second_shader_dll.fix: Delete the other shader DLL, keep only Bearforj.
bearforj.conflict.deformable_terrain.wha: Another deformable-terrain mod also changes landscape height; footprints will double or flicker.
bearforj.conflict.deformable_terrain.fix: Turn off Bearforj Terrain Deformation, or disable the other mod.
bearforj.conflict.footprints.what: Footprints mod also leaves prints; you get two sets.
bearforj.conflict.footprints.fix: Turn off Bearforj Terrain Deformation or the Footprints mod.
bearforj.conflict.particle_engine.what: Another precipitation/particle engine draws rain or snow too; precipitation doubles.
bearforj.conflict.particle_engine.fix: Turn off the other mod's rain/snow particles.
bearforj.conflict.embers.what: Embers mod adds fire embers; together with Bearforj spark particles fires look overloaded.
bearforj.conflict.embers.fix: Lower Physical Effect Particles, or keep only one embers mod.
bearforj.conflict.splashes.what: Splashes mod adds hit/rain splashes; Bearforj Physical Effect Particles does that too.
bearforj.conflict.splashes.fix: Turn off Physical Effect Particles or the other mod.
bearforj.conflict.fog_mod.what: Fog mod adds volumetric fog; with Height Fog it gets too thick.
bearforj.conflict.fog_mod.fix: Lower or turn off Bearforj Height Fog.
bearforj.conflict.wet_and_cold.what: Wet and Cold makes characters wet too; wetness doubles.
bearforj.conflict.wet_and_cold.fix: Turn off Submersion Wetness or Wet and Cold wetness.
bearforj.analyzer.tip_double_tm: Looks double-tonemapped: highlights never reach white and the image is flat. The weather mod probably tonemaps too - lower Bearforj tonemap mix.

bearforj.tune.enable: Turns this part on or off. If the picture does not change, restart the game, then press Save.
bearforj.tune.quality: Quality versus speed. Raise it a little at a time: the picture gets cleaner and the frame rate drops. Leave it near the default if you are unsure.
bearforj.tune.reach: How far the effect reaches. Larger values cover more of the scene and usually cost more. Move in small steps and watch the picture.
bearforj.tune.strength: How strong the effect is. Higher is more visible. If it looks fake, lower it toward the default.
bearforj.tune.limit: The point where the effect starts or stops. Nudge it until the artifact (halos, flicker, missing detail) goes away, then stop.
bearforj.tune.speed: How fast it changes. Faster reacts sooner and can flicker; slower looks smoother.
bearforj.tune.color: Color of this effect. Small shifts read as natural; big shifts look like a filter.
bearforj.tune.debug: A debug view. Turn it off while playing or the picture stays technical.
bearforj.tune.mode: Picks how the effect is calculated. Try the next entry, look at the picture, and keep the one that stays sharp without killing the frame rate.
bearforj.tune.generic: Tune this in small steps and watch the game picture. Stay near the default unless you know you want more or less of the effect, then press Save.

feature.cold_breath.name: Cold Breath
feature.cold_breath.description: Visible breath in snow and cold weather, using Wet and Cold's breath meshes.
feature.cold_breath.key_1: Plays on the head of the player, NPCs and a few creatures
feature.cold_breath.key_2: Only while it is snowing, out of doors
feature.cold_breath.credit: Breath meshes and textures are from Wet and Cold by isparks, CC BY-NC-SA.
feature.terrain_deformation.snow_raise_t: How far snow stands above the ground, in game units. Under the player it covers about 2.5 metres. The whole near field is only raised when that option is on.
feature.terrain_deformation.sand_raise_t: Shallow hollows in sand near the water are lowered, so small shore waves can wash them out.
feature.terrain_deformation.sink_tt: How much of the raised layer a foot presses down. 0.65 sinks about two thirds of the drift.
feature.water_waves.name: Water Waves
feature.water_waves.description: The water mesh is tessellated into swells. Wind, rain, depth and foam follow the weather. Far water stays flat.
feature.water_waves.key_1: Tessellated swells near the camera, flat past the range
feature.water_waves.key_2: Calm is a ripple, wind builds swells, storms add crest foam
feature.water_waves.key_3: Foam on the shore, on rocks and on the crests. Actors use the same height
feature.water_waves.amplitude_tt: Height of the longest wave, in game units, before the weather scales it. Calm wind keeps this small. It fades to a flat plane between 4000 and 7000 units.
feature.water_waves.shore_tt: How deep the water must be before the waves reach full height. The last 4 units at the beach stay flat, so the edge does not flicker.
feature.water_waves.tess_tt: Extra triangles near the camera, and only while the swell is large enough to need them. Calm water stays on the original mesh. At factor 1 the surface matches that mesh. Rivers and waterfalls are not moved.
feature.water_waves.foam_tt: White water on the shore, around rocks, and on storm crests. Crest foam grows with the wind.
feature.water_waves.detail_tt: Fine ripples on top of the swells. Two rotated samples of one normal map, so the pattern does not tile.

feature.skin.sweat_amount_tooltip: How strong the sweaty sheen is. It builds as stamina drops, and also while sprinting, fighting, or wearing heavy armor, then fades as stamina comes back. Face, neck and arms show it first. 0 turns sweat off.
feature.skin.sweat_starts_tooltip: Stamina fraction where the sheen starts. 0.75 means sweat begins once stamina falls below 75%.
feature.skin.full_sweat_tooltip: Stamina fraction where the sheen is fully on. 0.15 means full sweat below 15% stamina.
feature.wetness_effects.drying_speed_too: How fast skin, hair and armor dry after rain or wading. 1 is the dry time above. Drying is faster indoors, in sunlight, and next to a flame, and slower in snow or thick fog.
bearforj_look.tonemap_mix_tt: How much of the Bearforj tonemap is used on top of the game/weather tonemap. 100% with vanilla weathers; 15-40% with CS weather mods that ship their own filmic tonemap (NAT.CS, Obsidian CS, Vespro CS), so it is not applied twice. Weather profiles and presets set it automatically. Perf: ~0.
feature.gpu_footstep_particles.descripti: GPU-simulated dust, snow, mud clods and water splashes kicked up by footsteps.
feature.gpu_footstep_particles.key_1: Dust and clods on dirt, gravel, sand and ash; snow powder on snow
feature.gpu_footstep_particles.key_2: Wet mud clods in rain and on mud
feature.gpu_footstep_particles.key_3: Splashes scale with puddle and shallow water depth
feature.gpu_footstep_particles.key_4: Lit by the sun and ambient light, soft against the ground
feature.gpu_footstep_particles.name: GPU Footstep Particles
feature.physical_sky.add_light_scattered: Add light scattered by air (Aerial Perspective) to the scene.
feature.physical_sky.apply_additional_at:
Apply additional atmospheric tranmisttance on the directional light.
Introduces natural yellowening at sunset with white sunlight.
feature.physical_sky.breakup_tooltip: Separation between cloud bodies. Coverage stays fixed: the same cloud area is redistributed into fewer, denser bodies.
feature.physical_sky.character_tooltip: 0 = discrete convective cells, 1 = continuous stratiform sheets.
feature.physical_sky.cloud_map_presets_h: Presets only set the weather description. Map resolution, world size, centre, seed, and texture overrides are left unchanged.
feature.physical_sky.cloud_phase_model_d:
Dual-Lobe HG: the original two Henyey-Greenstein lobes driven by the eccentricity sliders below.
Approximate Mie: an HG + Draine numerical fit of Mie scattering for a water droplet, which reproduces the forward peak, fogbow and glory. It is physically parameterised, so the forward and backward eccentricity sliders do not affect it.
feature.physical_sky.cloud_scatter_integ:
Legacy: scalar 1 - exp(-sigma_s * ds) with a fixed 0.999 albedo, driven by luminance extinction.
Energy Conserving: the analytical per-channel form albedo * (1 - transmittance). Matches the coloured transmittance instead of a luminance-collapsed approximation; may need Scatter Source OD Scale retuning.
feature.physical_sky.cloud_size_tooltip: Horizontal diameter of a single convective cloud body.
feature.physical_sky.cloud_species_weigh: Weights are normalized within cloud-covered regions and biased by Instability. Set a weight to zero to disable that species.
feature.physical_sky.coverage_edge_width: Softness of the cloud edge. Cannot change how much sky is covered.
feature.physical_sky.description: Physically-based sky model for realistic sky gradients and other astronomical effects.
feature.physical_sky.dome_strength_toolt: How strongly a cloud thins toward its own edge. 0 produces flat slabs.
feature.physical_sky.enable_vanilla_clou: Enable vanilla cloud geometry rendering with Physical Sky relighting.
feature.physical_sky.enable_volumetric_c: Enable ray-marched volumetric clouds with NDF-based cloud shapes.
feature.physical_sky.generated_cloud_map: Generates weather, profile, cell, warp, and wisp textures on the GPU. Loaded DDS textures can override each generated input.
feature.physical_sky.high_coverage_toolt: Fraction of the sky carrying altostratus and altocumulus.
feature.physical_sky.instability_tooltip: Atmospheric instability. Higher values shift the species mix toward towering cumulus and cumulonimbus and deepen every cloud.
feature.physical_sky.key_feature_2: Procedural sun disk and celestial lighting controls.
feature.physical_sky.key_feature_3: Worldspace whitelist and interior override support.
feature.physical_sky.key_feature_4: Cloud relighting and silver lining controls.
feature.physical_sky.light_color_hint: This sets the light color BEFORE it goes through the atmosphere i.e. extraterrestrial radiance.
feature.physical_sky.light_step_distance: Fades the light-march step budget down to a single step with view distance, matching the erosion mip ramp (3 km to 100 km). 0 disables the LOD.
feature.physical_sky.multiplies_directio: Multiplies directional lighting applied to sky statics.
feature.physical_sky.name: Physical Sky
feature.physical_sky.overrides_the_color: Overrides the color of directional light. Linear tonemapper and 1.0 transmittance mix are recommended.
feature.physical_sky.particles_much_smal: Particles much smaller than the wavelength of light. They have almost complete symmetry in forward and backward scattering. On earth, they are what makes the sky blue and, at sunset, red. Usually needs no extra change.
feature.physical_sky.planet_radius_is_th:
Planet radius is the distance from the planet center to sea level.
Atmosphere radius is the distance from the planet center to the top of atmosphere.
On Earth, they are about 6360 km and 6420 km respectively.
feature.physical_sky.preset_broken_toolt: A lively convective sky. Larger cumulus with some towering development and moderate high cloud.
feature.physical_sky.preset_fair_tooltip: Scattered fair-weather cumulus. Small, well-separated, shallow clouds under a mostly clear sky.
feature.physical_sky.preset_front_toolti: An approaching warm front. Layered stratiform bands with an extensive altostratus veil above.
feature.physical_sky.preset_overcast_too: A continuous stratocumulus deck. Nearly full coverage, flat, with very little vertical development.
feature.physical_sky.preset_storm_toolti: Deep convection. Large, widely separated cells reaching cumulonimbus depth with heavy anvil outflow.
feature.physical_sky.real_world_sun_disk: Real world sun disk angular radius is about 0.27 degrees.
feature.physical_sky.remove_light_absorb: Remove light absorbed by air (Aerial Perspective) from the scene.
feature.physical_sky.sky_coverage_toolti: Fraction of the sky carrying low cloud. Solved exactly, so the value matches what you see.
feature.physical_sky.solid_and_liquid_pa: Solid and liquid particles greater than 1/10 of the light wavelength but not too much, like dust. Strongly anisotropic (Mie Scattering). They contributes to the aureole around bright celestial bodies.
feature.physical_sky.the_composition_and: The composition and physical properties of the atmosphere.
feature.physical_sky.the_ozone_layer_hig: The ozone layer high up in the sky that mainly absorbs light of certain wavelength. It keeps the zenith sky blue, especially at sunrise or sunset.
feature.physical_sky.the_sun_and_moons_a: The sun and moons, and their lights.
feature.physical_sky.tonemapper_is_force: Tonemapper is forced to Linear when Linear Lighting is enabled.
feature.physical_sky.treat_sky_statics_a: Treat sky statics as albedo and tint them with directional lighting.
feature.physical_sky.used_when_current_w: Used when current worldspace is not in whitelist (or worldspace data is unavailable), including forced interiors.
feature.physical_sky.usually_1_9_of_scat: Usually 1/9 of scatter coefficient. Dust/pollution is lower, fog is higher.
feature.physical_sky.weather_world_size_: Side length of one weather-map tile. The map repeats seamlessly, so this sets the scale at which the synoptic pattern recurs.
feature.skin.common_in_feature_settings: Common values are edited in the Advanced Skin feature settings.
feature.submersion_wetness.description: Characters get wet where they were in water and in the rain, then slowly dry.
feature.submersion_wetness.key_1: Wet line follows how deep the actor waded
feature.submersion_wetness.key_2: Beads and rivulets after leaving the water
feature.submersion_wetness.key_3: Rain soaks skin, armor and hair
feature.submersion_wetness.key_4: Works with Wetness Effects' character rain drops
feature.submersion_wetness.name: Submersion Wetness
feature.submersion_wetness.shelter_tt: Uses Skylighting's sky occlusion above each actor's head. Needs Skylighting enabled.
feature.terrain_deformation.description: Footprints are pressed into snow, mud and sand and slowly fill back in.
feature.terrain_deformation.grass_tt: Off by default: grass is not displaced, so pressing the ground under it would make it float.
feature.terrain_deformation.key_1: Footprints from the player and NPCs
feature.terrain_deformation.key_2: Real displacement with landscape tessellation near the camera
feature.terrain_deformation.key_3: Depth depends on the ground material; grass is left untouched
feature.terrain_deformation.name: Terrain Deformation
feature.terrain_deformation.raise_full_t: Off: snow, mud and sand stand only under your feet and in footprints. On: the raised layer covers the whole tessellation range.
feature.terrain_deformation.stride_fallb: Creates prints from movement for actors whose animations send no footstep events.
feature.terrain_deformation.tessellation: Really pushes the ground down near the camera. Without it the prints are only shaded.
feature.wetness_effects.wall_rain_enable: Water beads and narrow streams running down roofs, walls and rocks while it rains. Characters keep their own drops and trails.
